SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The mahāvākya verse — the culminating philosophical declaration of the Vairāgyaśataka. "Tattvamasi" (Thou art That — Chāndogya Upaniṣad) is the paradigmatic mahāvākya of Advaita. Bhartuhari ends this volume with the firm niścaya (certainty) of the non-dual position: Brahman alone is real; the world of multiplicity and change is appearance (mithyā — not simply false, but of a different order of reality). All the vairāgya, all the learning, all the love and renunciation of the three śatakas point to this.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: "तत्त्वमसि" इत्यादी महावाक्यांनी वारंवार जे सांगितलं जातं — ब्रह्मच एकमेव सत्य; जग मिथ्या — हाच दृढ निश्चय.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: "तत्त्वमसि" — तू तेच आहेस. हे महावाक्य वारंवार सांगितलं जातं कारण ते एकदा ऐकून समजत नाही — ते जगावं लागतं. ब्रह्म एकमेव सत्य, जग मिथ्या — हे अद्वैताचं सार. भर्तृहरिचे तीन शतके — नीती, शृंगार, वैराग्य — या एका निश्चयाकडे येतात. हाच अंतिम बोध.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
संसारविषवृक्षस्य द्वे फले अमृतोपमे ।
सुभाषितरसास्वादः सङ्गतिः सज्जनैः सह ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Saṃsāraviṣavṛkṣasya dve phale amṛtopame |
Subhāṣitarasāsvādaḥ saṅgatiḥ sajjanaiḥ saha ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: From the poison tree of worldly existence, there are two fruits that are like nectar: the tasting of beautiful utterances, and the company of the virtuous.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of surprising hope within the Nītiśataka's general realism. Saṃsāra is named a viṣavṛkṣa — a poison tree — and yet this tree bears two nectar-like fruits. The first is subhāṣitarasāsvāda — literally the savouring of well-spoken things, which encompasses poetry, wisdom literature, the pleasure of language used well. The second is the company of the virtuous. These two fruits make the poison tree worth inhabiting. The verse is quietly self-referential: the Nītiśataka itself is such a subhāṣita.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: संसाररूपी विषवृक्षाची दोन फळे अमृतासारखी आहेत: सुभाषितांचा रसास्वाद, आणि सज्जनांची संगत.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: संसार विषाचं झाड — पण त्याला दोन अमृतफळे आहेत. पहिलं: सुभाषित वाचणं, ऐकणं, चव घेणं. दुसरं: चांगल्या माणसांची संगत. हे दोन असतील तर विषाच्या झाडातही राहता येतं. भर्तृहरि हा श्लोक आशावादी आहे — जगणं सोपं नाही, पण या दोन गोष्टींमुळे सुकर होतं. आणि हे सुभाषित स्वतःच त्या पहिल्या फळाचं उदाहरण आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
पुस्तकेषु च या विद्या परहस्तगतं धनम् ।
कार्यकाले समुत्पन्ने न सा विद्या न तद्धनम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Pustaakeṣu ca yā vidyā parahastagatam dhanam |
Kāryakāle samutpanne na sā vidyā na taddhanam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Knowledge that remains only in books, and wealth that has gone into another's hands — at the time when action is needed, that is neither knowledge nor wealth.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse that draws a direct and precise parallel between two kinds of inaccessible resource. Knowledge locked in books — not absorbed, not practised, not integrated — is as inaccessible as wealth lent to someone who will not return it. When the moment of need arrives (kāryakāle samutpanne — when a situation arises requiring action), both fail equally. The verse is a practical argument for internalisation: knowledge must become part of the self, not merely a reference on a shelf.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: पुस्तकातच राहिलेली विद्या, आणि दुसऱ्याच्या हातात गेलेलं धन — कार्याची वेळ आली की ती विद्या नाही, ते धन नाही.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: पुस्तकातलं ज्ञान आणि परक्याकडचं धन — दोन्ही कामाच्या वेळी उपयोगी नाहीत. ज्ञान आतमध्ये उतरलेलं नसेल तर वापरता येत नाही. धन परत मिळणार नसेल तर संपत्ती नाही. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: शिकलेलं आत उतरवा, कमावलेलं जपा — नाहीतर दोन्ही व्यर्थ.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे तुष्यन्ति जन्तवः ।
तस्मात् तदेव वक्तव्यं वचने का दरिद्रता ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Priyavākyapradānena sarve tuṣyanti jantavaḥ |
Tasmāt tadeva vaktavyaṃ vacane kā daridratā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: All beings are pleased by the giving of pleasant speech. Therefore, speak only that — what poverty is there in words?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of generous practical wisdom. Pleasant speech — not flattery, but kind, considerate, affirming speech — costs nothing and pleases everyone. The question at the end is pointed: what poverty is there in words? Words are the one resource that does not diminish through giving. You do not become poorer by speaking kindly. Bhartuhari makes generosity of speech not merely a virtue but a practical philosophy: there is no reason not to be kind in speech, since it costs nothing and gives so much.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: प्रिय वाक्य बोलल्याने सगळे प्राणी तृप्त होतात. म्हणून तेच बोलावे — शब्दांत कसली दरिद्री?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: गोड बोलणं सगळ्यांना आनंद देतं — आणि ते मोफत आहे. शब्द बोलले तरी कमी होत नाहीत. मग गोड बोलण्यात कंजूषी का? भर्तृहरि विचारतो: शब्दांत दरिद्री नसते — मग मनमोकळेपणाने प्रिय बोला. हे व्यावहारिक उदारता आहे — ज्यात खर्च नाही, फायदा खूप.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
दुर्बलस्य बलं राजा बालानां रोदनं बलम् ।
बलं मूर्खस्य मौनित्वं चौराणां असतां बलम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Durbalasya balaṃ rājā bālānāṃ rodanam balam |
Balaṃ mūrkhasya maunivaṃ corāṇāṃ asatāṃ balam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The king is the strength of the weak; crying is the strength of children; silence is the strength of the foolish; and lying is the strength of the wicked and thieves.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of acute social observation. Each type of person has their characteristic weapon or resource. The weak have no power of their own — they are dependent on the king's justice. Children have no argument — they cry. The fool has no wisdom — but silence hides that (echoing the earlier verse on silence as ornament). The wicked have no legitimate claim — so they lie. Each group uses what they have, not what they ought to have. The verse is descriptive, not prescriptive — it maps the actual topography of social power.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: दुर्बलाचं बळ राजा; मुलांचं बळ रडणं; मूर्खाचं बळ मौन; आणि चोर-दुष्टांचं बळ असत्य.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: प्रत्येकाकडे जे आहे तेच वापरतो. दुर्बलाकडे राजाचं संरक्षण आहे, मुलाकडे अश्रू, मूर्खाकडे गप्प राहणं, दुष्टाकडे खोटेपणा. भर्तृहरि हे निष्पक्षपणे सांगतो — निंदा नाही, स्तुती नाही, फक्त निरीक्षण. समाजाचं हे वास्तवदर्शन शहाण्याला सांगतं: प्रत्येकाची 'शक्ती' ओळखा.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
प्रसादे सर्वमाप्नोति प्रसादे परमं सुखम् ।
प्रसादात् परमं श्रेयः प्रसादात् परमागतिः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Prasāde sarvamāpnoti prasāde paramaṃ sukham |
Prasādāt paramaṃ śreyaḥ prasādāt paramāgatiḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Through grace one obtains everything; through grace, supreme happiness. Through grace comes the highest good; through grace, the highest destination.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about prasāda — a multi-layered Sanskrit word meaning grace, favour, purity, clarity of mind. Four things come through prasāda: everything (sarvam), supreme happiness (paramaṃ sukham), the highest good (paramaṃ śreyas), and the highest destination (paramāgatiḥ). Whether this refers to divine grace, the teacher's grace, or the inner quality of mental purity and clarity — all three readings are valid in the Indian tradition. Bhartuhari places this as a reminder that effort alone is not sufficient: openness to grace completes the picture.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: प्रसादाने सगळं मिळतं; प्रसादाने परम सुख. प्रसादाने परम श्रेय; प्रसादाने परम गती.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: प्रसाद — कृपा, स्वच्छता, प्रसन्नता. चार गोष्टी प्रसादाने येतात — सगळं, परम सुख, परम श्रेय, परम गती. प्रयत्न महत्त्वाचा — पण प्रसाद (गुरूची, देवाची, किंवा आत्मशुद्धीची कृपा) त्याला पूर्ण करतो. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: मेहनत करा, पण त्यापलीकडचं कृपेने येतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
कुचेलिनं दन्तमलोपधारिणं
बह्वाशिनं निष्ठुरभाषिणं च ।
सूर्योदये चास्तमने च शायिनं
विमुञ्चति श्रीरपि चक्रपाणिम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kucelinaṃ dantamalopadhāriṇaṃ
Bahvāśinaṃ niṣṭurabhāṣiṇaṃ ca |
Sūryodaye cāstamane ca śāyinaṃ
vimuñcati śrīrapi cakrapāṇim ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: One who wears dirty clothes, who keeps filth on the teeth, who eats excessively, who speaks harshly, and who sleeps at sunrise and sunset — even Viṣṇu himself would be abandoned by Lakṣmī for these.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of practical conduct advice delivered through a striking theological image. Even Viṣṇu — the sustainer of the universe, Lakṣmī's eternal consort — would lose her presence if he exhibited these five qualities: slovenliness, poor oral hygiene, gluttony, harsh speech, and sleeping through the two sacred junctions of the day. Lakṣmī (wealth, prosperity, grace) is a guest who must be attracted and maintained through dignity of living. The verse makes self-care a spiritual practice.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: घाणेरडे कपडे घालणारा, दातांवर मळ ठेवणारा, जास्त खाणारा, कठोर बोलणारा, सूर्योदय आणि सूर्यास्ताला झोपणारा — अशा विष्णूलाही लक्ष्मी सोडून जाईल.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: विष्णूलाही लक्ष्मी सोडेल — जर हे पाच दोष असतील. हे अतिशयोक्ती आहे, पण संदेश स्पष्ट आहे: श्रीसंपत्ती, यश, लक्ष्मी — ते स्वच्छता, संयम, गोड वाणी, आणि वेळेच्या पालनाने राहतात. जगणं नीटनेटकं असेल तर लक्ष्मी टिकते. भर्तृहरिचा हा सल्ला अगदी व्यावहारिक आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
परस्परस्य मर्माणि ये भाषन्ते नराधमाः ।
त एव विलयं यान्ति वल्मीकोदरसर्पवत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Parasparasya mārmāṇi ye bhāṣante narādhamāḥ |
Ta eva vilayaṃ yānti valmīkodārasarpavat ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Those lowest of people who expose each other's vulnerabilities — they destroy themselves, like snakes inside an anthill.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A vivid image of self-destruction through mutual betrayal. Snakes inside an anthill — a confined space with multiple dangerous occupants — inevitably turn on each other. The people (narādhama — lowest of humans) who reveal each other's secrets, who use intimate knowledge as weapons — they are like those snakes: their mutual destruction is inevitable. Bhartuhari's observation is not moral but structural: betrayal as a mode of relationship destroys all parties, not just the betrayed.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: एकमेकांच्या दुखऱ्या जागा उघड करणारे नराधम लोक वारुळातल्या सापांसारखे स्वतःच नष्ट होतात.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: वारुळात सापांसारखे. बंदिस्त जागेत एकमेकांवर डसत राहतात — आणि सगळे नष्ट होतात. जे लोक एकमेकांची दुखरी रहस्ये उघड करतात ते असेच असतात. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: हे फक्त नैतिक दोष नाही — हे व्यावहारिक आत्मनाश आहे. विश्वासघात करणारे स्वतःचं घर जाळतात.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
पद्माकरं दिनकरो विकचं करोति
चन्द्रो विकासयति कैरवचक्रवालम् ।
नाभ्यर्थितो जलधरोऽपि जलं ददाति
सन्तः स्वयं परहिताय विधेर्नियुक्ताः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Padmākaraṃ dinakaaro vikacaṃ karoti
Candro vikāsayati kairavacakravālam |
Nābhyarthito jaladharo'pi jalaṃ dadāti
santaḥ svayaṃ parahitāya vidheraniyuktāḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The sun opens up the bed of lotuses; the moon causes the circle of water-lilies to bloom; the rain cloud gives water even without being asked. The good are naturally appointed by fate itself to work for others' benefit.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of natural order as ethical paradigm. The sun does not choose to open the lotus — it simply does what it is. The moon does not decide to bloom the water-lily — it simply shines. The cloud does not wait to be asked before raining. These natural processes are used to define the sant (good person) — one who works for others' benefit not from calculation or duty but from nature. Fate itself (vidhi) has appointed them to this. It is who they are.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: सूर्य कमळांचा तलाव उमलवतो; चंद्र कुमुदांचा समूह उमलवतो; न मागताच मेघ पाणी देतो; सज्जन विधीनेच परोपकारासाठी नियुक्त झालेले असतात.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: निसर्गातून नीती. सूर्याला कमळासाठी ठरवून यावं लागत नाही — तो उजाडतो आणि कमळ उमलतात. चंद्राला सांगावं लागत नाही — तो उगवतो आणि कुमुद फुलतात. मेघाला विनंती नाही — तो पडतो आणि पाणी देतो. सज्जन असेच असतात — त्यांचं अस्तित्व परोपकार आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः ।
नास्ति रागसमं दुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Nāsti vidyāsamaṃ cakṣurnāsti satyasamaṃ tapaḥ |
Nāsti rāgasamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti tyāgasamaṃ sukham ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: There is no eye equal to knowledge; no austerity equal to truth; no suffering equal to attachment; no happiness equal to giving up.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: Four comparative statements, each precise. Knowledge is the eye — it allows one to see the world as it is. Truth is the greatest austerity — maintaining it under all circumstances is harder than any physical discipline. Attachment (rāga) is the greatest suffering — not loss, not pain, but the clinging itself. And giving up (tyāga) is the greatest happiness — not renunciation as deprivation, but the relief and expansiveness of releasing what one was clinging to.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: विद्येसारखा डोळा नाही; सत्यासारखं तप नाही; रागासारखं दुःख नाही; त्यागासारखं सुख नाही.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: चार तुलना — चार सत्ये. ज्ञान हे खरे डोळे — जग जसे आहे तसे दाखवतात. सत्य हे खरे तप — सगळ्या परिस्थितीत टिकवणे कठीण. आसक्ती हे खरे दुःख — गमावणे नाही, धरणे. आणि त्याग हे खरे सुख — सोडण्यातला विस्तार. भर्तृहरिचे हे चार सूत्र आयुष्यभर पुरतात.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
आयुः कल्पतरोश्च कोमलदलं वाताहतं कम्पते
लक्ष्मीर्जलतरङ्गचञ्चलतरा विद्युल्लताचञ्चला ।
आयुः स्वप्नसमं यशः कुसुमवत् सौभाग्यमुन्मीलितं
चिन्त्यं सारमतो हि किं बत नरैः प्राप्तेन जन्मान्तरे ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Āyuḥ kalpataroś ca komaladale vātāhataṃ kampate
Lakṣmīrjalataraṃgacañcalatarā vidyullatācañcalā |
Āyuḥ svapnasamaṃ yaśaḥ kusumaavat saubhāgyamunmīlitaṃ
cintyaṃ sāramato hi kiṃ bata naraiḥ prāptena janmāntare ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Life trembles like a tender leaf of the wish-fulfilling tree struck by wind; Lakṣmī is more restless than a water-ripple, more fleeting than a flash of lightning; life is like a dream, fame like a flower, good fortune something that has just opened. What then, O humans, is the essence to be sought in this life obtained after countless births?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of escalating impermanence images, culminating in the essential question. The kalpavṛkṣa (wish-fulfilling tree) has a tender leaf — and even that trembles at the wind. Lakṣmī (prosperity) is more unstable than ripples, more fleeting than lightning. Life: a dream. Fame: a flower. Fortune: newly opened (and therefore about to close). The question at the end is not rhetorical despair but genuine philosophical inquiry: given all this, what is the sāra — the essence, the marrow — worth pursuing?
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: आयुष्य वाऱ्याने हलणाऱ्या कल्पवृक्षाच्या कोवळ्या पानासारखं कापतं; लक्ष्मी लाटेहूनही चंचल, विजेहूनही क्षणिक; जीवन स्वप्नासारखं, यश फुलासारखं, सौभाग्य नुकतं उमललेलं. तर, माणसांनो, असंख्य जन्मांनी मिळालेल्या या जन्मात सार काय मिळवायचे?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: अनित्यतेच्या प्रतिमांचा हा कळस. कल्पवृक्षाचं पानही कापतं. लक्ष्मी लाटेपेक्षाही अस्थिर. जीवन स्वप्न, यश फूल, सौभाग्य नुकतं उमललेलं. आणि मग प्रश्न: असंख्य जन्मांनी मिळालेल्या या मनुष्यजन्मात खरोखर काय साधायचे? हा प्रश्न उत्तराची अपेक्षा करतो — वैराग्याच्या दिशेत.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
उपदेशो हि मूर्खाणां प्रकोपाय न शान्तये ।
पयःपानं भुजङ्गानां केवलं विषवर्धनम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Upadeśo hi mūrkhāṇāṃ prakopāya na śāntaye |
Payaḥpānaṃ bhujaṅgānāṃ kevalaṃ viṣavarddhanam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Instruction to the foolish only increases their anger — it does not calm them. Giving milk to serpents only increases their poison.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse that complements the earlier "sandbank oil" and "crocodile fangs" verses, using a new and striking image. Milk — the purest, most nourishing of substances — fed to a serpent does not nourish or calm the snake; it only increases the venom. Similarly, instruction and wisdom given to the fundamentally foolish does not illuminate them; it aggravates their resistance and increases their self-justifying aggression. The verse advises discernment about where teaching energy is spent.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: मूर्खांना उपदेश राग वाढवतो, शांती आणत नाही. सापाला दूध पिणं केवळ विष वाढवतं.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: सापाला दूध — शुद्धतम गोष्ट — दिलं तरी त्याचं विष वाढतं. मूर्खाला ज्ञान दिलं तर राग येतो. हे क्रूर नाही — हे व्यावहारिक. जे उपदेश घेण्याच्या स्थितीत नाहीत त्यांना उपदेश देण्यात ऊर्जा वाया जाते. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: शिकवण्याआधी शिकणारा तयार आहे का हे पाहा.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
किं तत्र बहुनोक्तेन शास्त्रकोटिशतेन वा ।
दुर्जनः सज्जनो नैव यावज्जीवं स्थितिः सदा ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kiṃ tatra bahunokten śāstrakotiśatena vā |
Durjanaḥ sajjano naiva yāvajjīvaṃ sthitiḥ sadā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: What is the use of saying much, or of hundreds of crores of scriptures? The wicked person never becomes virtuous — that state persists for a lifetime.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of frank pessimism about moral transformation. The rhetorical opening — "what is the use?" — signals impatience with the comforting fiction that all people can be improved by sufficient education or scripture. Bhartuhari's observation is empirical: the durjana (wicked person) is wicked throughout life. This does not mean people cannot change — but that fundamental character rarely does. The verse is paired with "svabhāvo nopadeśena" (No. 163) to form a consistent position on the limits of external influence.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: जास्त बोलण्याचा किंवा कोटी-शेकडो शास्त्रांचा काय उपयोग? दुर्जन सज्जन कधी होत नाही — जन्मभर तीच स्थिती.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: हे कठोर सत्य आहे. शास्त्रे, उपदेश, शिक्षण — सगळं दिलं तरी जो मुळातच वाईट आहे तो बदलत नाही. स्वभाव खोल असतो. भर्तृहरि याबद्दल स्पष्ट आहे: दुर्जनावर वेळ आणि शक्ती वाया घालवणे सोडा. हे वास्तव स्वीकारणं हेच शहाणपण.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
किं वा बलं राजमतौ पराक्रमे
किं पण्डिते किं बहुभाषिते गुणः ।
क्षमावतां तेजसि किं विशेषणं
सर्वं सहेत क्षमया च पण्डितः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kiṃ vā balaṃ rājamtau parākrame
Kiṃ paṇḍite kiṃ bahubhāṣite guṇaḥ |
Kṣamāvatāṃ tejasi kiṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ
sarvaṃ saheta kṣamayā ca paṇḍitaḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: What is the value of strength in the matter of kings and valour? What is the quality of the learned person? What virtue is there in speaking much? The radiance of the patient — what word describes it? The truly learned person bears everything with patience.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse that raises and quietly answers questions about the highest virtue. Each question peels away a lesser claim — physical strength, scholarship, eloquence — before landing on kṣamā (patience, forbearance, forgiveness). The "radiance of the patient" (kṣamāvatāṃ tejas) is presented as something beyond ordinary description. And the paṇḍita (truly learned person) is ultimately defined by their capacity to bear everything with patience — not by their knowledge alone.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: राज्यात बळाचं महत्त्व काय? पंडिताचा गुण काय? जास्त बोलण्यात काय? क्षमावंतांच्या तेजाचं वर्णन काय? खरा पंडित क्षमेने सगळं सहन करतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: प्रत्येक प्रश्नाने एक दाव्याची सोलाई होते. बळ, विद्वत्ता, वाक्चातुर्य — सगळ्यांपेक्षा क्षमा वरती. क्षमावंताचे तेज वर्णन करण्यापलीकडे आहे. आणि खरा पंडित? — तो सगळं सहन करतो क्षमेने. ज्ञान एकट्याने पुरत नाही — ते क्षमेने पूर्ण होतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
दातृत्वं प्रियवक्तृत्वं धीरत्वमुचितज्ञता ।
अभ्यासेन न लभ्यन्ते चत्वारः सहजा गुणाः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Dātṛtvaṃ priyavaktṛtvaṃ dhīratvamucitatajñatā |
Abhyāsena na labhyante catvāraḥ sahajā guṇāḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Generosity, pleasant speech, courage, and knowing what is appropriate — these four qualities are innate and cannot be acquired by practice.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about sahaja guṇas — innate qualities. The four named — giving, agreeable speech, steadiness, and situational appropriateness — are either in a person's nature or they are not. They can be imitated but not truly acquired through drill. This does not mean education is useless — it cultivates many things — but that these four particular qualities have a different, deeper root. A person born with them has a kind of grace not available to those who must work at it artificially.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: दानशीलता, प्रियभाषण, धीरता, आणि योग्य-अयोग्य जाणणं — हे चार गुण जन्मजात आहेत, अभ्यासाने मिळत नाहीत.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: काही गुण शिकता येतात, काही येत नाहीत. दान, गोड बोलणं, धाडस, प्रासंगिकता — हे जन्मजात असतात. अभ्यास खूप गोष्टी देतो — पण या चार गोष्टी मूळ स्वभावातून येतात. ज्याला जन्मजात आहेत त्याला एक विशेष कृपा आहे. हे जाणून स्वतःतलं ओळखा — आणि इतरांतलं आदरा.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
सम्पूर्णकुम्भो न करोति शब्दम्
अर्धो घटो घोषमुपैति नूनम् ।
विद्वान् कुलीनो न करोति गर्वम्
गुणैर्विहीना बहु जल्पयन्ति ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Sampūrṇakumbho na karoti śabdam
Ardho ghaṭo ghoṣamupaikti nūnam |
Vidvān kulīno na karoti garvam
Guṇairvihīnā bahu jalpayanti ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: A fully filled pot makes no sound. The half-filled pot certainly makes a noise. The learned and well-born do not show pride. Those without virtue chatter abundantly.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The full-and-empty pot image — one of the most universally understood similes in Indian wisdom literature. The full pot is silent because it is complete. The half-empty one rattles and sloshes with every movement. The learned and virtuous person has no need to advertise themselves — their fullness is self-evident to those with eyes. Those empty of virtue compensate with noise. The verse is among the most quoted in Bhartuhari's corpus.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: भरलेला घडा आवाज करत नाही; अर्धा घडा नक्कीच घुमतो. विद्वान आणि कुलीन माणूस गर्व दाखवत नाही; गुणहीन लोक जास्त बडबड करतात.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: भरलेला घडा शांत, अर्धा घुमतो — हे सगळ्यांना माहीत आहे. माणसाचंही तसंच. खऱ्या विद्वानाला जाहिरात नको — त्याची पूर्णता स्वतः बोलते. रिकामे लोक जास्त बोलतात — भरून दाखवायचं असतं. भर्तृहरिचा हा श्लोक सर्वात स्मरणीय आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
वदनं किसलयरागं नयनं नवनीलोत्पलं ।
कुचौ च घनसारभासौ बाहू च मृणालकोमलौ ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Vadanaṃ kisalayarāgaṃ nayanaṃ navanīlotpalaṃ |
Kucau ca ghanasārabhāsau bāhū ca mṛṇāllakomalau ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The face — red as a new leaf; the eye — a freshly blossomed blue lotus; the breasts — with the lustre of camphor masses; the arms — soft as lotus stalks.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of pure lyrical description — the classical Sanskrit śṛṅgāra portrait in its most concentrated form. Four body parts, four plant/flower comparisons: the red leaf for the warm-tinted face, the blue lotus for the deep dark eye, camphor for the pale luminous breast, the lotus stalk for the soft arm. Each comparison works in multiple dimensions — colour, texture, quality. The verse is meant to be savoured slowly, each comparison held separately before the whole is assembled.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: मुख — नव्या पानाची लालिमा; नयन — नव्या निळ्या कमळासारखे; स्तन — कापुराच्या तेजासारखे; बाहू — मृणालासारखे कोमल.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: शृंगाराचं हे शास्त्रीय चित्र. चार अंगे, चार उपमा — प्रत्येक वेगळ्या दिशेने सौंदर्य पकडते. नव्या पानाची लालिमा — उबदार. निळ्या कमळाचे डोळे — खोल, गहन. कापूर — शुभ्र तेजस्वी. मृणाल — अत्यंत कोमल. भर्तृहरि येथे चित्रकारासारखा रंगवतो — एक एक रेषा हळुवारपणे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
स्त्रीणां प्राणाधिको भर्ता तस्मात् स्त्रीणां परं सुखम् ।
विवाहादि क्रियाः कृत्वा पतिमेव प्रपूजयेत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Anupameya sā preyasī mama dhanyā yā mama
Smṛtipathe vilasati ca sadā |
Na hi sā nayane paśyāmi
tāṃ kimu vā vadāmi manasā bata cetasā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: My incomparable beloved — she who is fortunate for me, who always shines on the path of my memory. I do not see her with my eyes — what can I say? In the mind, in the heart, she is.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of memory as presence. The beloved is not visible to the eyes — but she is always vivid on the path of memory (smṛtipatha). Bhartuhari draws a distinction between two kinds of seeing: ocular (nayane) and inner (manasā cetasā — with the mind and heart). The beloved who is absent from sight is fully present in the mind. The verse captures something precise: memory is not a pale substitute for presence but a different and sometimes more vivid form of presence.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: माझ्यासाठी भाग्यशाली ती — माझी अतुलनीय प्रिया — जी नेहमी माझ्या स्मृतीपथावर विलसते. डोळ्यांनी तिला पाहत नाही — काय सांगू? — मनाने, हृदयाने ती आहे.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: डोळ्यांनी नाही, मनाने. स्मृतिपथावर नेहमी. आठवण ही उपस्थितीची एक वेगळी रीत आहे — कमी नाही, कधीकधी अधिक. ती दूर आहे, पण मन-हृदयात पूर्ण आहे. भर्तृहरि येथे प्रेमाच्या अंतःसृष्टीचं वर्णन करतो — जे डोळ्यांपलीकडे असतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
गाढालिङ्गनविग्रहाः क्षणमपि व्यावृत्तचित्ता न ते
जातास्तीव्रविरागिणः पुनरपि स्वप्नान्तरे दर्शिताः ।
रूपं याति विलोचनाभिरमतां प्राणान् दधाति प्रिया
कामः किं करोतीति भावयति मां दह्यानलस्तापयेत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Gāḍhāliṅganavigrahāḥ kṣaṇamapi vyāvṛttacittā na te
Jātāstīvravirāgiṇaḥ punarapi svapnāntare darśitāḥ |
Rūpaṃ yāti vilocanābhiramataṃ prāṇān dadhāti priyā
Kāmaḥ kiṃ karotīti bhāvayati māṃ dahyānalastāpayent ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Those who were held in close embrace — their minds never turned away even for a moment; they are shown again in the intervals of sleep. The beloved's form delights the eyes; she holds the very breaths. What does Kāma do? — he burns me with the fire of burning, he heats me.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of helpless desire — desire as something that happens to the lover, not something chosen. The memories of embrace return in dreams. The beloved holds the breaths — literally sustains life. And through all of this, Kāma burns. The double construction "dahyānalastāpayat" — burning with the fire of burning — is deliberate: it is not that desire causes discomfort; desire is itself an active fire that perpetually burns.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: गाढ आलिंगनात असलेले — त्यांचे मन एका क्षणासाठीही हटले नाही; ते स्वप्नाच्या अंतरालातही पुन्हा दिसतात. प्रियेचं रूप डोळ्यांना आनंदवतं; प्राण धारण करतं. काम काय करतो? — तो जाळत राहतो, धगधगवत राहतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: आलिंगनाच्या आठवणी स्वप्नातही येतात. प्रिया श्वास धारण करते — म्हणजे ती नसेल तर श्वासही नाही. काम म्हणजे फक्त इच्छा नाही — तो आग आहे. "जाळत राहतो, धगधगवत राहतो" — दोन क्रिया, एकच यातना. भर्तृहरि कामाला निव्वळ भावना नाही तर एक अस्तित्व म्हणून दाखवतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
पीतं त्वया यदि मया मधु तुल्यमेव
अथवा कृतं नवजलार्द्रपटेन गात्रम् ।
यद्वा त्वया स्मितमिव स्फुटतारकाढ्यं
किं नाम तत्र विषमं मनसः प्रसङ्गः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Pītaṃ tvayā yadi mayā madhu tulyameva
Athavā kṛtaṃ navajalārdrpaṭena gātram |
Yadvā tvayā smitamiva sphuṭatārakāḍhyaṃ
kiṃ nāma tatra viṣamaṃ manasaḥ prasaṅgaḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: If you have drunk honey and I have drunk it equally — or if the body has been cooled with fresh wet cloth — or if you have smiled like a sky full of clearly visible stars — what unequal thing is there in the mind's attachment to this?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of erotic philosophy — justifying the mind's attachment by the equality of shared experience. The honey drunk together, the cooling cloth applied together, the shared smile like a starry sky — these shared experiences create an equality that makes the mind's attachment perfectly understandable. The question "what is unequal in the mind's attachment?" is a defence of desire: if both have shared the same beauty, how can attachment to it be wrong?
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: तू आणि मी दोघांनी सारखंच मधु प्याले; किंवा नव्या ओल्या कपड्याने देह थंड केला; किंवा तारकांनी भरलेल्या आकाशासारखं तू हसलीस — मग मनाच्या आसक्तीत असमान काय आहे?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: दोघांनी एकच अनुभव घेतला — मग आसक्ती का अयोग्य? भर्तृहरि प्रेमाचा बचाव करतो — तात्विकपणे. साझा केलेलं मधु, साझा केलेली थंडाई, साझा हास्य — यातून आसक्ती नैसर्गिक आहे. हे शृंगाराचं तर्कशास्त्र — प्रेमाला न्याय्य ठरवणं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
धनिकः श्रोत्रियो राजा नदी वैद्यस्तु पञ्चमः ।
पञ्च यत्र न विद्यन्ते न तत्र दिवसं वसेत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Dhanasya mārgaṃ yadi vakti vaktā
Vaktur mahatvādavadhāryatāṃ tat |
Priyāpriye svapnasamāni vitta-
mante naro vijñatayopabhoge ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: If a speaker speaks of the path of wealth, let that be understood from the greatness of the speaker. Wealth is like a dream — at the end the person enjoys it with understanding, both the pleasant and the unpleasant.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about the relationship between wisdom and wealth — and the ultimate equanimity with which the truly knowing person relates to both. The wise speaker can speak of wealth's path, but their authority comes from their realisation that wealth is ultimately dream-like: the pleasant and unpleasant phases are equally illusory. The vijñatā (the person of understanding) enjoys life's experiences — both pleasure and pain — with this background knowledge of their dream-like quality.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: वक्ता धनाचा मार्ग सांगत असेल तर त्याच्या महत्त्वाने ते स्वीकारा. धन स्वप्नासारखं आहे — शेवटी ज्ञानी माणूस प्रिय आणि अप्रिय दोन्ही समभावाने उपभोगतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: धनाचा मार्ग सांगणारा महत्त्वाचा — पण त्याचा संदेश हा: धन स्वप्न आहे. ज्ञानी माणूस हे जाणतो आणि म्हणून सुख-दुःख दोन्ही समभावाने घेतो. शृंगारशतकात हे येतं कारण प्रेम, धन, सुख — सगळं स्वप्नासारखं. हे जाणून जगणं हे खरं जगणं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
अतिपरिचयादवज्ञा सन्ततगमनादनादरो भवति ।
मलये भिल्लपुरन्ध्री चन्दनतरुकाष्ठमिन्धनं कुरुते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Atiparicayādavajñā santagamanādanādaro bhavati |
Malaye bhillapurandhrī candanatarukāṣṭhaminddhanaṃ kurute ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: From excessive familiarity comes contempt; from constant visiting comes disregard. The tribal woman of the Malaya mountain uses sandalwood as firewood.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about the corrosion of familiarity. The sandalwood — the most precious and fragrant of woods — becomes mere firewood to the woman who lives surrounded by it. She no longer smells its fragrance or recognises its value. The extraordinary has become the ordinary. Bhartuhari uses this to counsel a kind of conscious preservation of distance and freshness in relationships: closeness, when unmodulated, breeds contempt.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: अतिपरिचयाने अवमान होतो; सतत येण्याने अनादर. मलय पर्वतावरची भिल्ल स्त्री चंदनाचं लाकूड जळण म्हणून वापरते.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: चंदन — सर्वात मौल्यवान सुगंधी लाकूड — पण मलयपर्वतावरच्या स्त्रीसाठी फक्त जळण. ती त्याचा सुगंध ओळखत नाही कारण ती त्यात बुडालेली आहे. खूप जवळ असलेलं मूल्य कमी होतं. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: अंतर राखणं हे संबंधातील आदर टिकवतं. अतिसान्निध्य मूल्य नाश करतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
अश्नन्नपि न तृप्यन्ति विषयाः पञ्च पञ्चभिः ।
विद्यमानेऽपि संतोषे सुखं लभ्यं न केनचित् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Aśnannapi na tṛpyanti viṣayāḥ pañca pañcabhiḥ |
Vidyamāne'pi santoṣe sukhaṃ labhyaṃ na kenacit ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Even by feeding them with the five sense objects, the five senses are never satisfied. Even when contentment is present, happiness is not obtained by anyone.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about the structural impossibility of satisfaction through sense objects. The five senses fed by five corresponding sense objects — the eye with form, the ear with sound, and so on — are never satiated. Hunger increases with feeding. And — the second and more subtle observation — even when contentment (santoṣa) is apparently present, genuine happiness (sukha) eludes everyone. Contentment as a concept is not the same as the living experience of happiness. True sukha comes from within, not from sense-satisfaction.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: पाच विषयांनी पाच इंद्रियांना खायला घातलं तरी ती तृप्त होत नाहीत. संतोष असला तरी खरं सुख कोणाला मिळत नाही.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: इंद्रिये कधी तृप्त होत नाहीत — खाल्लं की भूक वाढते. आणि मग दुसरं — संतोष असला तरी सुख नाही. संतोष ही संकल्पना आहे, सुख हा अनुभव आहे. फरक महत्त्वाचा. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: बाहेरून सुख शोधण्याचा मार्ग बंद आहे — आत शोधा.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
अयमेव हि साधूनां शिक्षणं सम्मतं बुधैः ।
सत्यवादिषु भावो यः सत्यसाधनकारकः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Cumbantaḥ priyamukhamindīvaradalaśyāmam
Svīyāṃ candanacarcitāmapi tanūm |
Āliṅgantaḥ stanatatim sphuritasaukhyam
te kṛtārtham iti manyante pṛthivīm ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Kissing the beloved face dark as blue lotus petals; embracing one's own body anointed with sandalwood; pressing that breast trembling with happiness — they who do this think the earth well-rewarded.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of erotic fulfilment — the Śṛṅgāraśataka's most direct celebration of physical love. The three acts — the kiss, the embrace of the sandalwood-anointed body, the pressing of the breast — are described with lyrical precision, and the philosophical conclusion is that those who have known this have found their earth well-rewarded (kṛtārtham). The earth exists for such moments of genuine physical and emotional union.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: नीलकमळाच्या पाकळीसारख्या श्यामल प्रियेचं मुख चुंबन घेत; चंदन-लेपित अंगाला कवटाळत; सुखाने थरथरणाऱ्या स्तनांना स्पर्श करत — असे करणारे पृथ्वीला सार्थ मानतात.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: प्रेमाच्या शारीरिक पूर्णतेचं हे साक्षात सांगणं. चुंबन, आलिंगन, स्पर्श — तीन क्रिया, एक पूर्णता. आणि मग: हे जगणं सार्थ आहे. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: असे प्रेमक्षण हेच पृथ्वीचं सत्य. शृंगारशतकात हे उत्कट मांडणं धाडसाचं आणि प्रामाणिक आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
मुखं पद्ममिवाभाति यस्याः कण्ठश्च शङ्खवत् ।
सा देवी मम हृदये तिष्ठति सुखदायिनी ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Mukhampaddmamivābhāti yasyāḥ kaṇṭhaśca śaṅkhavat |
Sā devī mama hṛdaye tiṣṭhati sukhadāyinī ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: She whose face shines like a lotus and whose throat is like a conch — that goddess dwells in my heart, the giver of happiness.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A simple, beautiful verse of devotional love. The beloved is named "devī" — goddess — and her dwelling place is the poet's heart. The lotus-face and conch-throat are classical comparisons (both associated with auspiciousness and the divine). By calling her goddess and locating her in the heart rather than in the world, Bhartuhari suggests that the beloved transcends the merely physical — she has become a deity of the inner life. This is the point where śṛṅgāra touches bhakti.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: जिचं मुख कमळासारखं चमकतं आणि कंठ शंखासारखा — ती देवी माझ्या हृदयात राहते, सुखदायिनी.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: प्रिया देवी बनते. कमळमुख, शंखकंठ — दोन्ही मंगल, दैवी प्रतीके. ती देवी आहे आणि हृदयात वास करते. भर्तृहरि शृंगाराला भक्तीशी जोडतो — प्रेम आणि पूजा एकाच मार्गावर भेटतात. जी व्यक्ती हृदयात देवतेसारखी वास करते, ती केवळ प्रेमपात्र नाही — ती पूज्य आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
रहसि सम्भृतहासकलाकुला
कुचकलशविलग्नवसत्रया ।
विरचितापरपार्श्वनिवेशना
प्रियतमा मम चेतसि राजते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Rahasi sambhṛtahāsakalākulā
kucakalaśavilagnavasatrayā |
Viracitāparapārśvaniveśanā
priyatamā mama cetasi rājate ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: In a private place, overflowing with suppressed laughter; her garment caught on the pitcher of her breast; arranged in a posture facing the other side — my beloved shines in my mind.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of extraordinary intimacy — not erotic action but erotic situation: the beloved in a private moment, laughing with suppressed delight, her garment accidentally caught, turned slightly away. The image is of a particular domestic intimacy — unguarded, natural, half-seen. Bhartuhari captures the kind of beauty that only the beloved sees: not the public presentation but the private, slightly dishevelled, laughing presence. This shines in the mind.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: एकांतात दडवलेल्या हास्याने भरलेली; स्तनकलशावर अडकलेल्या वस्त्राने; दुसऱ्या बाजूला वळलेल्या मुद्रेत बसलेली — माझी प्रिया माझ्या मनात चमकते.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: हे उत्कट वर्णन नाही — हे घरगुती, हळुवार, अर्धे पाहिलेले आहे. एकांतात हसणारी, वस्त्र अडकलेलं, थोडी बाजूला वळलेली. हे असं चित्र आहे जे फक्त प्रियकर पाहतो — सार्वजनिक नाही, खासगी. आणि हेच मनात राजते. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: खरं प्रेम या निरागस, असुरक्षित क्षणांत असतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
प्रियः पृच्छति कः पन्था इत्युक्ते पथिकेन सः ।
तदा पान्था इव ज्ञात्वा हर्षाद् रोदिति बालिशा ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Priyaḥ pṛcchati kaḥ panthā ityukte pathikena saḥ |
Tadā pāntha iva jñātvā harṣādroditi bāliśā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: When the traveller passes and asks "which is the road?" — she, hearing the word "traveller" (pāntha), thinking of her beloved who is also a traveller, weeps with joy.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of supreme psychological delicacy. The beloved woman hears a passing stranger ask for directions — uses the word pāntha (traveller). She hears the word and immediately, involuntarily, thinks of her beloved who is also a pāntha — a wanderer away from home. The word alone, in an innocent context, triggers tears of emotion — tears not of sorrow but of sudden, overwhelming remembering. This is how love works: a single word, a scent, a sound, unlocks the floodgates.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: एक वाटसरू "कोणता रस्ता?" असं विचारतो — त्यात "पान्था" (वाटसरू) शब्द ऐकून ती सरळ हर्षाने रडते, कारण तिचा प्रियकरही प्रवासी आहे.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: एका शब्दाने प्रेम जागं होतं. अनोळखी माणूस रस्ता विचारतो — त्यात "पान्था" हा शब्द. तिच्या प्रियकराचाही हाच शब्द — प्रवासी. आणि ती रडते — आनंदाने, अचानक. हे प्रेमाचं सत्य आहे: एक शब्द, एक सुगंध, एक आवाज — आणि संपूर्ण अनुभव परत येतो. भर्तृहरि हे क्षण पकडतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
प्रथितयशसां भर्तृदारिद्र्यदुःखं
जगति बहवो भान्ति क्लेशाः शरीरे ।
मणिरपि महान् काञ्चनाश्रित्य राजते
गुणवदगुणं याति संसर्गयोगात् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Prathitayaśasāṃ bhartuḥ dāriddryaduḥkhaṃ
jagati bahavo bhānti kleśāḥ śarīre |
Maṇirapi mahān kāñcanāśritya rājate
guṇavadaguṇaṃ yāti saṃsargayogāt ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The sorrow of the husband's poverty is great for those of renowned families; many sorrows shine in the world and in the body. Even a great gem shines by being set in gold; through association with the virtuous, even the unvirtuous gains virtue.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of social observation and optimistic possibility. The first half names a specific sorrow: the wife of a renowned family suffering her husband's poverty — a double humiliation of expectation and reality. But the second half opens outward: even a gem needs gold to shine at its best, and even a person of poor virtue can acquire it through good association. The verse moves from constraint to possibility without denying the pain of the first.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: यशस्वी कुळातील स्त्रीसाठी पतीचं दारिद्र्य मोठं दुःख; जगात आणि शरीरात अनेक क्लेश दिसतात. मोठा मणी सोन्यात जडल्यावर शोभतो; सत्संगाने गुणहीनही गुणवंत होतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: दोन प्रतिमा. पहिली: श्रेष्ठ कुळातील स्त्री दरिद्री पतीमुळे दुखावते — हे विशिष्ट सामाजिक वेदना. दुसरी: मणी सोन्यात शोभतो, सत्संगाने माणूस सुधारतो. पहिल्या भागाची वेदना मान्य करून दुसरा भाग आशा देतो: संदर्भ बदलतो — माणूस सुधारतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
नित्यं निःसृमरत्नसंगतिरयं नित्यं सुवर्णायते
वारं वारमपि प्रसन्नललितं नित्यं नवं दृश्यते ।
एतत् प्रेमविलासमण्डनमयं चित्रं च नेत्रोत्सवं
देव्याः कोऽपि विभूषणेन विभुते तस्मै नमः कारणम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Nityaṃ niḥsṛmaratna-saṃgatir-ayaṃ nityaṃ suvarṇāyate
Vāraṃ vāramapi prasannalalitaṃ nityaṃ navaṃ dṛśyate |
Etat premavilāsanamandanamayaṃ citraṃ ca netrotsavaṃ
devyāḥ ko'pi vibhūṣaṇena vibhute tasmai namaḥ kāraṇam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Always in contact with precious gems, always gold-like; seen again and again, always clear, lovely, always fresh. This adorned with the play of love's ornaments — wondrous, a festival for the eyes — with the goddess's ornament shining through, salutation to whatever is the cause of this.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of aesthetic wonder — the wonder that beauty exists at all, that the beloved is always fresh however many times seen, that her ornaments catch and give back light, that love's play adorns her. The final gesture — "salutation to whatever is the cause of this" — is Bhartuhari refusing to name the cause (whether God, nature, fate, or simply beauty itself) and instead bowing to it in gratitude. The unknown cause of beauty deserves salutation.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: नेहमी रत्नांच्या संगाने सुवर्णासारखी; वारंवार पाहिली तरी नेहमी नवी, प्रसन्न, सुंदर. प्रेमविलासाच्या अलंकारांनी सजलेली — चित्र, नेत्रांचा उत्सव — देवीच्या तेजाने उजळलेली. ज्याने हे कारण आहे त्याला नमस्कार.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: सौंदर्याचं आश्चर्य — "ज्याने हे घडवलं त्याला नमस्कार." भर्तृहरि कारण नाव घेत नाही — तो फक्त झुकतो. सौंदर्याचं मूळ अज्ञात आहे — पण ते आहे, हे जाणतो. वारंवार पाहिलेलं नेहमी नवं वाटणं — हे प्रेमाचं रहस्य. आणि त्या रहस्याला नमस्कार.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
कान्ता कटाक्षविशिखाः करिणीकराभाः
बाहुप्रसारणपरा हृदयैकलक्ष्याः ।
एते वयस्य विरहे मम दीर्घरात्रीं
कामस्य बाणनिकराः कुरुते प्रहाराम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kāntā kaṭākṣaviśikhāḥ kariṇīkarābhāḥ
bāhuprasāraṇaparā hṛdayaikalakṣyāḥ |
Ete vayasya virahe mama dīrgharātrīṃ
kāmasya bāṇanikārāḥ kurute prahārām ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The glances of the beloved — arrows, elephant-trunk like arms extended, aimed only at the heart — these, O friend, during my long night of separation, are the arrows of Kāma raining down blows.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse that maps the beloved's physical attributes onto Kāma's weapons. The sidelong glance becomes a flying arrow; the extended arms like elephant trunks become Kāma's quiver. In the long night of separation, these remembered physical images become active weapons — they do not comfort but wound. The beloved is absent but her remembered gestures are present as blows. Memory here is not consolation but its opposite.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: प्रियेचे कटाक्ष बाण आहेत; हत्तींच्या सोंडेसारखे बाहू पसरवत; फक्त हृदयाला लक्ष्य करत — हे मित्रा, विरहाच्या माझ्या दीर्घ रात्री कामाच्या बाणांचे हल्ले करतात.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: आठवणी जखम करतात. प्रिया नाही — पण तिचे कटाक्ष, तिचे बाहू — हे आठवणीत बाण बनतात. विरहाच्या रात्री जास्तच. मित्राला सांगतो कारण एकट्याने सहन होत नाही. भर्तृहरि विरहाची ही विशिष्ट यातना — आठवणीच आघात करतात हे — अचूक पकडतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
यद्यत् परिणतं स्वाद्वि तद्रसस्यावताराय ।
यद्यत् कदर्थितं भूयस्तद्रसस्योत्तराय नः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Mugdhāyāḥ prathamam pariṇaya niśi sā yā stutiḥ
Yā lajjā prathamasmitena militā |
Sā śayyā virahāt tadāśritaśarīrasambhavā
Svapne'pi smarati tadā rame ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: That praise on the first night of the innocent bride's marriage; that shyness joined with a first smile; that bed arising from the body that rested there in their absence — even in dreams she remembers then, I take delight.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of wedding-night memory — the innocence, the shyness, the first smile, the bed that retains the body's warmth after separation. The verse is from the woman's perspective in dream: remembering the first night, the first timid meeting, and even the empty bed that carries memory of the beloved. Dreams become the space where these memories are revisited. Bhartuhari's sensitivity here is extraordinary.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: त्या भोळ्या वधूच्या पहिल्या विवाहरात्रीची स्तुती; पहिल्या हास्यासोबत लज्जा; ते पलंग जे विरहात त्या शरीराच्या आठवणीने भरलेले — स्वप्नात तिला ते आठवते आणि मला आनंद होतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: पहिल्या रात्रीच्या आठवणी — स्तुती, लज्जा, पहिलं हास्य. आणि मग पलंग — जो रिकामा आहे पण शरीराची उष्णता धारण करतो. स्वप्नात ती आठवते. हे सूक्ष्म, कोमल आहे — भर्तृहरिचं शृंगार येथे अत्यंत हळुवार आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
पयोधरौ हेमकुम्भसमप्रभौ
बिम्बाधरौष्ठं च सुधाविलासि ।
नखेन लिखितं चकास्ति ललाटे
भर्तुः स्मृतौ किल नारी प्रसीदति ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Payodharau hemaakumbhasamaprabhau
bimbādharauṣṭhaṃ ca sudhāvilāsi |
Nakhena likhitam cakāsti lalāṭe
bhartuḥ smṛtau kila nārī prasīdati ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The breasts — with the lustre of golden pitchers; the lips — playing with nectar; a mark written by a nail shines on the forehead — at the remembrance of her husband, the woman is indeed pleased.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of intimate domestic beauty — the mark of love on the forehead, the remembered husband, the woman pleased by memory alone. The nail-mark (nakhena likhitam) on the forehead is a classical sign of love's night — left by the beloved's hand. When she remembers her husband, even that mark seems to shine more brightly. Memory activates what physical presence made — the mark of love responds to the remembrance of the lover.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: स्वर्णकुंभासारखे तेजस्वी स्तन; अमृतसाखळे ओठ; कपाळावर नखाने काढलेलं चिन्ह चमकतं — पतीची आठवण आल्यावर स्त्री प्रसन्न होते.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: पतीच्या आठवणीने ते नखचिन्हही उजळतं. हे प्रेमाचं चिन्ह — रात्रीच्या जवळिकेतून आलेलं — आठवण आल्यावर अधिक चमकतं. भर्तृहरि येथे सांगतो: प्रेम चिन्हांत राहतं — शरीरावर, मनात — आठवणीने जागं होतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
इदं शरीरं परिणाममेयं
इदं च नाम प्रसरत् यशांसि ।
अयं च कालः परिवर्तमानः
कः पण्डितोऽत्र स्वहितं न कुर्यात् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Idaṃ śarīraṃ pariṇāmameyaṃ
idaṃ ca nāma prasarat yaśāṃsi |
Ayaṃ ca kālaḥ parivartamānaḥ
kaḥ paṇḍito'tra svahitaṃ na kuryāt ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: This body — measurable by its end; this name — spreading as fame; this time — revolving. What wise person here would not work for their own highest good?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of urgency within the Śṛṅgāraśataka — the erotic context gives way to the existential. The body has a finite measure (pariṇāma — transformation, end). The name/reputation spread as fame has its own trajectory. Time revolves — it does not stop. Given all three, what wise person would not attend to their ultimate self-benefit (svahita — one's own highest good, which is not selfish but the pursuit of one's genuine long-term welfare)? The question is not rhetorical — it is an invitation.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: हे शरीर — अंताने मापलेलं; हे नाव — यश म्हणून पसरणारं; हा काळ — फिरणारा. इथे कोणता पंडित स्वतःचं हित करणार नाही?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: शरीर, नाव, काळ — तिन्ही चालत्या गोष्टी. शरीराला अंत आहे, नाव यश-अपयशात फिरतं, काळ थांबत नाही. मग हे जाणून कोणता शहाणा माणूस स्वतःच्या खऱ्या हितासाठी काम करणार नाही? — म्हणजे मुक्तीसाठी, उच्च जगण्यासाठी. हे प्रश्न उत्तराची अपेक्षा करतो: तुम्ही.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
काचः काञ्चनसंसर्गाद् धत्ते मारकतीं द्युतिम् ।
तथा सत्संगतिः पुंसां मूर्खाणामपि मुक्तिदा ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kācaḥ kāñcanasaṃsargād dhatte mārakatīṃ dyutim |
Tathā satsaṅgatiḥ puṃsāṃ mūrkhāṇāmapi muktidā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Glass, through association with gold, takes on the lustre of an emerald. In the same way, the company of the virtuous gives liberation even to fools.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The final verse of the Śṛṅgāraśataka's main section — and it is not an erotic verse but a philosophical one. Glass next to gold takes on an emerald-green glow: it does not become gold, but it acquires a beauty it could never have alone. The company of the virtuous transforms even the most unpromising person — not by making them virtuous instantly, but by allowing their dormant better nature to reflect the quality nearby. Even fools, Bhartuhari says, can attain liberation through such association.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: काचेला सोन्याच्या संगाने पाचूसारखी चमक येते. त्याप्रमाणे सत्संगती मूर्खांनाही मुक्ती देते.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: काच स्वतः मौल्यवान नाही — पण सोन्याशेजारी पाचूसारखी दिसते. माणसाचंही असंच. मूर्ख माणूसही सत्संगतीत मुक्त होऊ शकतो. हे आशावाद आहे — सगळ्यांसाठी दरवाजा आहे. शृंगारशतक हे प्रेमाने सुरू झाले आणि या आशेने संपते.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
कुसुमस्तबकस्येव द्वे गती परिकीर्तिते ।
मूर्ध्नि वा सर्वलोकस्य विशीर्येत वनेऽथवा ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kusumastabakasyeva dve gatī parikīrtite |
Mūrdhni vā sarvalokasya viśīryeta vane'thavā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: For a bunch of flowers, two destinies are spoken of: either to rest on the heads of all people, or to wither in the forest.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of two noble paths. The bunch of flowers (kusumastabaka) has exactly two honourable fates: adorning the head (being used in service, worship, offering) or withering naturally in the forest (renouncing the world without being made into an object of use). There is no third path — the flower does not belong in a rubbish heap or in ignoble use. For the gifted person, Bhartuhari implies, the same choice exists: either serve actively in the world or retire into pure renunciation. What is not acceptable is a mediocre middle.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: फुलांच्या गुच्छाच्या दोन गती सांगितल्या आहेत: एकतर सर्व लोकांच्या माथ्यावर विराजणं, नाहीतर वनात कोमेजणं.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: फुलांचे दोन सन्मानित मार्ग — माथ्यावर पूजा होणं किंवा वनात स्वाभाविकपणे कोमेजणं. तिसरा नाही. माणसाचंही तसंच — एकतर जगात सेवेत, नाहीतर वनात वैराग्यात. मध्यमार्ग नाही. भर्तृहरि मध्यमार्गाला नाकारतो — एकतर पूर्ण जगा, नाहीतर पूर्ण सोडा.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
हर्तुर्याति न गोचरं किमपि शं पुष्णाति यत्सर्वदा
ह्यर्थिभ्यः प्रतिपाद्यमानमनिशं प्राप्नोति वृद्धिं पराम् ।
कल्पान्तेष्वपि न प्रयाति निधनं विद्याख्यमन्तर्धनं
येषां तन्नृपसत्तमैः सह नरैः कस्माद् भवेद् गौरवम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Harturyāti na gocaraṃ kimapi śaṃ puṣṇāti yatsarvadā
hyarthibhyaḥ pratipādyamānamanishaṃ prāpnoti vṛddhiṃ parāṃ |
Kalpānteṣvapi na prayāti nidhanaṃ vidyākhyamantarddhanaṃ
yeṣāṃ tannṛpasattamaiḥ saha naraiḥ kasmādbhaved gauravāṃ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: What cannot come within the thief's sight; what always nourishes goodness; what given to seekers constantly attains the highest growth; what does not perish even at the dissolution of an age — that internal wealth called knowledge. Why should those who possess it revere even the best of kings?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse that goes further than the famous "na corahāryam" verse (No. 99) — it asks not just what knowledge is, but what it implies for the relationship between knowledge and power. Those who possess this indestructible, ever-growing, theft-proof wealth — why should they bow even to the greatest king? The question is not arrogance but a genuine repositioning of value: the wealth of knowledge exceeds the wealth of kingdoms.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: जे चोराच्या नजरेस येत नाही; जे नेहमी चांगलं पोषण करतं; याचकांना दिल्याने अधिक वाढतं; युगांतानंतरही नष्ट होत नाही — ते विद्यारूपी आंतरधन. ज्यांच्याकडे हे आहे, ते उत्तम राजांनाही का नमतील?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: विद्येचा हा गौरव नीतिशतकाहूनही पुढे जातो. राजांनाही नमण्याची गरज नाही विद्यावंताला — कारण त्याची संपत्ती राजाहूनही मोठी. आणि हे गर्वाने नाही — ते मूल्यांच्या सत्य मापनाने. विद्याधन खरोखरच सर्वश्रेष्ठ.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
मृत्पिण्डे च घटोत्पत्तिर्मृत्पिण्डे च विनश्यति ।
यथा घटो मृदां भेदो तथात्मा परमात्मनि ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Mṛtpiṇḍe ca ghaṭotpattiḥ mṛtpiṇḍe ca vinaśyati |
Yathā ghaṭo mṛdāṃ bhedo tathātmā paramātmani ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: In clay the pot is born; in clay it is destroyed. As the pot is merely a modification of clay — so the individual self is in the supreme Self.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The pot-clay analogy is the most classical image in Advaita Vedānta for the relationship between the individual self and the absolute. The pot appears to be separate — it has a name, a shape, a function. But it is entirely clay: born from clay, returning to clay, made of nothing but clay. In the same way, the jīvātman (individual self) is a modification (bheda — differentiation, not separation) of the paramātman (supreme Self). The pot is not annihilated when it returns to clay — it simply loses its false separateness.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: मातीच्या गोळ्यातून घडा जन्मतो; मातीतच नष्ट होतो. जसा घडा मातीचाच भेद, तसाच आत्मा परमात्म्यात.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: घडा-माती — अद्वैताचं सर्वात प्रसिद्ध उदाहरण. घडा वेगळा वाटतो — नाव, रूप, उपयोग. पण तो संपूर्ण माती आहे. परत गेला की माती होतो. जीवात्मा तसाच — परमात्म्याचा भेद, वेगळा नाही. परत जाणं म्हणजे नाश नाही — खोट्या वेगळेपणाचा अंत.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
रात्रिर्गमिष्यति भविष्यति सुप्रभातं
भास्वानुदेष्यति हसिष्यति पङ्कजश्रीः ।
इत्थं विचिन्तयति कोशगते द्विरेफे
हा हन्त हन्त नलिनीं गज उज्जहार ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Rātrirgamiṣyati bhaviṣyati suprabhātaṃ
bhāsvānudeṣyati hasiṣyati paṅkajaśrīḥ |
Itthaṃ vicintayati kośagate dvirephhe
hā hanta hanta nalinīṃ gaja ujjahāra ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: "The night will pass; a beautiful dawn will come; the sun will rise; the lotus will bloom with beauty" — while the bee within the lotus was thinking thus, alas, alas — the elephant uprooted the lotus.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: One of the most poignant verses in the entire Vairāgyaśataka. The bee, enclosed in the lotus blossom at nightfall, thinks optimistically: dawn will come, the sun will rise, the flower will open. While it plans for a tomorrow that seems inevitable — the elephant comes and uproots the whole lotus. No dawn for the bee. The verse is about the supreme danger of postponing spiritual practice, thinking there is always more time. The elephant of death does not wait for the bee's plans.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: "रात्र जाईल, सुंदर पहाट होईल, सूर्य उगवेल, कमळ हसेल" — असा विचार करत कमळात बसलेल्या भुंग्याला — हाय, हाय — हत्तीने कमळासकट उपटलं.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: भुंगा योजना करतो — उद्या चांगलं होईल. पण हत्ती आधी येतो. भर्तृहरिचा हा श्लोक वैराग्याच्या तातडीबद्दल आहे. "उद्या करीन" — हे भुंग्यासारखं विचार करणं. मृत्यूरूपी हत्ती वाट पाहत नाही. उद्या सांगत बसू नका — आजच करा.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
यदा किंचित्कर्ता भवति पुरुषो यत्नपरवशो
विकर्ता तत्सर्वस्य भवति च विधाता बलवता ।
तदा चित्तं खिद्येदपि किमु न कर्तव्यमिति तत्
ततोऽन्यत्र त्यागे भजनमपरे तत्त्ववचनम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Yadā kiṃcittkartā bhavati puruṣo yatnaparavaśo
vikartā tatsarvasya bhavati ca vidhātā balavatā |
Tadā cittaṃ khidyedapi kimu na kartavyamiti tat
tato'nyatra tyāge bhajanamapare tattvavacanaṃ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: When a person becomes a doer of something through effort and circumstance, but the powerful creator undoes all of it — then the mind is distressed: "what then is to be done?" Beyond this, in renunciation, is devotion; and beyond that, the word of truth.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about the experience of futility — when sustained effort is undone by forces beyond one's control. The mind asks the deepest question: then what is to be done? Bhartuhari's answer moves in two stages: tyāga (renunciation — giving up the insistence on one's effort producing results) and bhajana (devotion, alignment with the divine) and beyond that, tattva-vacana — the word of truth, the highest teaching. The path from frustration to liberation moves through these three stages.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: माणूस प्रयत्नाने काहीतरी करतो — पण बलवान विधाता सगळं उलटवतो. तेव्हा मन व्याकुळ होतं: "मग करायचं काय?" — त्यापलीकडे त्यागात भजन आहे; त्यापलीकडे तत्त्वाचा शब्द.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: प्रयत्न केला — विधात्याने उलटवलं. मन विचारतं: काय करायचं? भर्तृहरि तीन टप्पे सांगतो: त्याग (फळाची आसक्ती सोड), भजन (देवाशी जुळवून घे), आणि तत्त्वज्ञान (खरं सत्य जाण). निराशेतून मुक्तीकडे हा मार्ग.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
संसारसागरं तर्तुं को नो नौकां समाश्रयेत् ।
सत्सङ्गतिर्नौका प्रोक्ता संसारार्णवतारिणी ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Saṃsārasāgāraṃ tartuṃ ko no naukāṃ samāśrayet |
Satsaṅgatirnoukā proktā saṃsārārṇavatāriṇī ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: To cross the ocean of existence — who would not take shelter in a boat? The company of the virtuous is declared the boat that carries one across the ocean of worldly existence.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The simplest and most direct statement of the śataka's recurring counsel. Saṃsāra is an ocean — deep, wide, stormy. To cross it, one needs a boat. The boat is satsaṅgati — the company of the truly virtuous. The image is complete: you cannot swim across alone; you need the craft of wisdom embodied in others. The previous verse (No. 201) opened this volume with the same satsaṅgati teaching — Bhartuhari returns to it here in its most compressed form.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: संसारसागर तरण्यासाठी कोण नौकेचा आश्रय घेणार नाही? सत्संगती ही संसारसागर पार करवणारी नौका सांगितली आहे.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: संसार समुद्र — खोल, रुंद, वादळी. एकट्याने पोहता येत नाही — नौका लागते. ती नौका म्हणजे सत्संगती. या खंडाची सुरुवात सत्संगतीने झाली (व्ही. २०१) — इथे ती नौकेच्या रूपात परत येते. भर्तृहरिचा हा संदेश वारंवार येतो: सत्संगती जगण्याचं सर्वात मोठं साधन.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
ईश्वरः कारणं पुंसां योगसंयोगहेतुषु ।
संसारस्तु क्रियाहेतुः फलहेतुः स उच्यते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritā yena sarvaṃ
sākṣī cetā kevalo nirguṇaśca |
Nityo'ntaḥstho nirguṇas tattvameva
vijñāyainaṃ mucyate sarvabanddhaiḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The experiencer, the experienced, and that which motivates all — the witness, pure consciousness, alone, beyond qualities, eternal, dwelling within, without attributes — knowing this truth, one is freed from all bonds.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of pure Sāṃkhya-Vedānta synthesis. The three: bhoktā (experiencer/puruṣa), bhogyam (the experienced/prakṛti), and preritā (the motivating force). Then the description of the transcendent: sākṣī (witness), cetā (consciousness), kevala (alone, independent), nirguṇa (beyond the three qualities), nitya (eternal), antaḥstha (dwelling within), without attributes. To know this truth is to be freed from all bonds. This is perhaps the most philosophically dense verse in the Vairāgyaśataka.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: भोक्ता, भोग्य, आणि जे सगळ्यांना प्रेरित करतं — साक्षी, चेतना, केवळ, निर्गुण, नित्य, आत राहणारं, गुणांपलीकडे — हे तत्त्व जाणून माणूस सर्व बंधांतून मुक्त होतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: सांख्य-वेदांताचं सार. तीन: अनुभवणारा, अनुभव, आणि प्रेरणादायक. आणि त्यांच्या पलीकडे: साक्षी, चेतना, एकटं, निर्गुण, नित्य, आत राहणारं. हे जाणलं की सगळं सुटतं. भर्तृहरिचं हे तत्त्वज्ञान घन आहे — पण त्याचा अर्थ सोपा: जाणण्यातच मुक्ती.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां शरीरं साधनं यतः ।
तस्य स्वास्थ्यं विना किं स्यात् फलं पुण्येन केनचित् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ śarīraṃ sāddhanaṃ yataḥ |
Tasya svāsthyaṃ vinā kiṃ syāt phalaṃ puṇyena kenacit ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Since the body is the instrument for dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa — without its health, what fruit can any merit yield?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of practical wisdom about the body. In the Vairāgyaśataka — a book about renunciation — Bhartuhari makes a sophisticated argument: the body is not the obstacle to liberation but its instrument (sādhana). All four puruṣārthas (dharma, artha, kāma, mokṣa) are accomplished through the body. Without bodily health (svāsthya), no merit yields fruit. Renunciation does not mean neglecting the body — it means not clinging to it while maintaining it well.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: धर्म, अर्थ, काम आणि मोक्ष यांचं साधन शरीर आहे. त्याच्या आरोग्याशिवाय कोणत्या पुण्याचं फळ मिळेल?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: वैराग्यशतकात शरीराचं महत्त्व. शरीर त्यागाचा विषय नाही — ते साधन आहे. धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष — चारही शरीराने होतात. शरीर निरोगी नसेल तर कोणत्याच गोष्टींचं फळ नाही. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: शरीरावर आसक्ती नको, पण त्याची काळजी हवी — कारण ते साधन आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
वृद्धत्वं जरयात्येति रूपं हरति च क्रमात् ।
आयुः क्षयति कालेन नाशयत्यायुषः शरत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Vṛddhatvaṃ jarayātyeti rūpaṃ harati ca kramāt |
Āyuḥ kṣayati kālena nāśayatyāyuṣaḥ śarat ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Old age comes through ageing and gradually takes away beauty. Life is depleted by time — and autumn destroys summer's life.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of quiet, inevitable decline. Old age comes through ageing itself — a tautology that is not meaningless but precise: age causes ageing, which causes more ageing. Beauty leaves gradually (kramāt — step by step). Life is depleted by time. And then the striking seasonal image: autumn destroys what summer built — the harvest season carries within it the dissolution of the lush growth. The verse does not mourn; it simply observes the universal arc.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: वृद्धत्व जराने येतं, रूप हळूहळू जातं. आयुष्य काळाने क्षीण होतं — शरद ऋतू उन्हाळ्याच्या आयुष्याचा नाश करतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: हळूहळू, अटळपणे — वय येतं, रूप जातं, आयुष्य क्षीण होतं. शरद ऋतू उन्हाळ्याला संपवतो — जे बहरलं ते कोमेजतं. भर्तृहरि यावर शोक करत नाही — तो बघतो. या दृष्टीतच वैराग्याचं बीज आहे. बदल अपरिहार्य आहे — हे जाणणं मुक्ती देतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
रे रे चातक सावधानमनसा मित्र क्षणं श्रूयतां
अम्भोदा बहवो हि सन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैतादृशाः ।
केचिद् वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति धरणीं गर्जन्ति केचिद् वृथा
यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Re re cātaka sāvdhānamanasā mitra kṣaṇaṃ śrūyatāṃ
Ambhodā bahavo hi santi gagane sarve'pi naitādṛśāḥ |
Kecid vṛṣṭibhirārdrayanti dharaṇīṃ garjanti kecid vṛthā
Yaṃ yaṃ paśyasi tasya tasya purasto mā brūhi dīnaṃ vacaḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: O cātaka bird, listen carefully for a moment, O friend — many clouds exist in the sky, but not all of them are the same. Some moisten the earth with rain; some thunder uselessly. To whoever you see — do not speak a word of supplication before all of them.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The cātaka — the mythological bird that drinks only rainwater from a specific cloud — is an emblem of discriminating devotion. Bhartuhari addresses it directly with wise counsel: there are many clouds, but they are not equal. Some give real rain; some only thunder. Do not supplicate before every cloud you see — choose the one that actually gives. Applied to human life: choose your teachers, mentors, and guides carefully; not everyone who thunders delivers.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: अरे चातका, एक क्षण सावध होऊन ऐक, मित्रा — आकाशात अनेक ढग आहेत, पण सगळे सारखे नाहीत. काही पावसाने जमीन ओलावतात, काही उगाचच गडगडतात. जो जो दिसेल त्याच्यासमोर दीन वाचा बोलू नकोस.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: चातक फक्त स्वाती नक्षत्राचा पाऊस पितो — विशिष्ट ढगाचाच. भर्तृहरि त्याला सल्ला देतो: सगळे ढग सारखे नाहीत. काही खरोखर पाऊस देतात, काही फक्त गडगडतात. प्रत्येकासमोर विनंती करू नकोस. माणसाच्या जीवनात: शिक्षक, मार्गदर्शक निवडताना सावध रहा — गडगडणारे आणि पाऊस देणारे वेगळे असतात.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
अजरामरवत् प्राज्ञो विद्यामर्थं च चिन्तयेत् ।
गृहीत इव केशेषु मृत्युना धर्ममाचरेत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Ajarāmaravat prājño vidyāmarthaṃ ca cintayet |
Gṛhīta iva keśeṣu mṛtyunā dharmamācaret ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The wise person should pursue knowledge and wealth as if he were immortal — and practise dharma as if death had already seized him by the hair.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of magnificent double instruction. The first movement: pursue knowledge and wealth with the long-term commitment of someone who will never die — without hurry, without cutting corners, with patient depth. The second movement: practise dharma as if death's hand is already in your hair right now — with absolute urgency, without postponement. The combination is not contradictory but complementary: plan for eternity, act for this moment.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: शहाण्या माणसाने विद्या आणि धन अजरामर असल्यासारखे मिळवावेत; आणि धर्माचं आचरण मृत्यूने केशांना धरल्यासारखं करावं.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: दोन सूचना एकत्र. विद्या आणि धन मिळवणं — जणू मरणार नाही असं. दीर्घकालीन, खोलवर, घाई न करता. धर्माचं आचरण — जणू मृत्यू आत्ताच केसांना धरलाय असं. तातडीने, आत्ता, उशीर न करता. दोन्ही एकत्र: अनंत काळासाठी योजना, क्षणाला कृती.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
जातीयसंयोगवशेन जीवाः
संयान्ति योनिं पुनरेव सर्वे ।
अन्तः कषायं परिशोध्य भानोः
किरणा इव स्वच्छतया विशन्ति ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Jātīyasaṃyogavaśena jīvāḥ
saṃyānti yoniṃ punareva sarve |
Antaḥ kaṣāyaṃ pariśodhya bhānoḥ
kiranā iva svacchatayā viśanti ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Through the force of connection with their kind, all beings return again to the womb. Having purified the inner impurity — like the rays of the sun, they enter in purity.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about the cycle of rebirth and the possibility of breaking it through inner purification. All beings return to the womb (are reborn) through the force of their accumulated tendencies (kāṣāya — inner impurity, residue of karma). But those who have purified this inner residue are compared to sunbeams — they enter (dissolve into the source) with the clarity and purity of light. The purified soul does not return — it merges, like light returning to the sun.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: स्वजातीय संयोगाच्या बळाने सगळे प्राणी पुन्हा योनीत जातात. पण आतलं कषाय शुद्ध केल्यावर सूर्याच्या किरणांसारखे स्वच्छतेने विलीन होतात.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: पुनर्जन्म आणि मुक्ती. सगळे प्राणी परत येतात — कारण आतले संस्कार ओढतात. पण ज्याने आतली अशुद्धता साफ केली, तो सूर्यकिरणांसारखा — स्वच्छपणे, प्रकाशाने — विलीन होतो. परत येत नाही. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: मोक्ष म्हणजे परत न येणं — स्वच्छतेने सूर्यात विरणं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
इच्छा सती कुरुते दुःखं तत्त्यागः सुखकारणम् ।
सुखस्य हेतुः संतोषः तृष्णा दुःखस्य कारणम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Icchā satī kurute duḥkhaṃ tattyāgaḥ sukakāraṇam |
Sukhasya hetuḥ santoṣaḥ tṛṣṇā duḥkhasya kāraṇam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Desire present causes suffering; its abandonment is the cause of happiness. The cause of happiness is contentment; craving is the cause of suffering.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of four elegant propositions about desire and happiness. The first pair: desire causes suffering; its abandonment causes happiness. The second pair: contentment causes happiness; craving causes suffering. The four together form a closed logical system: contentment and the absence of desire are the same thing; craving and the presence of desire are the same thing. Happiness and suffering are not determined by circumstances but by the mind's relationship to desire.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: इच्छा असल्याने दुःख होतं; तिचा त्याग सुखाचं कारण. सुखाचं कारण संतोष; तृष्णा दुःखाचं कारण.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: चार सत्ये, बंद वर्तुळ. इच्छा = दुःख. इच्छात्याग = सुख. संतोष = सुख. तृष्णा = दुःख. म्हणजे: संतोष आणि इच्छात्याग एकच; तृष्णा आणि इच्छा एकच. सुख परिस्थितीत नाही — मन इच्छेशी कसं नातं ठेवतं यावर अवलंबून. भर्तृहरिचं हे सूत्र बौद्ध तत्त्वज्ञानाशीही जुळतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
एकाकी निःस्पृहः शान्तः पाणिपात्रो दिगम्बरः ।
कदा शान्तमनाः शैले रमिष्यामि निरामयः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Ekākī niḥspṛhaḥ śāntaḥ pāṇipātro digambaraḥ |
Kadā śāntamanāḥ śaile ramiṣyāmi nirāmayaḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Alone, desireless, peaceful, with the hand as begging bowl, sky-clad — when will I, with a quiet mind, take delight in the mountain, free from all disease?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of longing for the renunciant life — one of the most personal in the Vairāgyaśataka. The poet is not yet in that state but longs for it: no possessions, no desire, no illness of body or mind, alone in the mountain. The hand as the begging bowl is the image of absolute simplicity — nothing to carry, nothing to lose. The question "when?" expresses that this is aspiration, not accomplishment. The most honest verses in the śataka are these ones of longing.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: एकटं, निःस्पृह, शांत, हातच पात्र, दिगंबर — कधी शांत मनाने, रोगमुक्त होऊन, पर्वतावर रमेन?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: हे वैराग्यशतकातलं सर्वात प्रामाणिक श्लोक. भर्तृहरि म्हणत नाही "मी असाच आहे" — तो म्हणतो "कधी होईन?" हे अजून झालेलं नाही — हे स्वप्न आहे, ध्येय आहे. एकटं, निःस्पृह, हात पात्र, आजारांशिवाय, पर्वतावर. इच्छाशिवाय फक्त एक इच्छा — या निःस्पृह अवस्थेची.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
तावद् भयस्य भेतव्यं यावद्भयमनागतम् ।
आगतं तु भयं दृष्ट्वा प्रहर्तव्यमभीतवत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Tāvad bhayasya bhetavyaṃ yāvadbhayamanāgatam |
Āgataṃ tu bhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā prahartavyamabhītavat ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Fear should be feared only as long as it has not arrived. But when fear has come and is seen — strike it without flinching, as the fearless do.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: This verse appeared in the Śṛṅgāraśataka (Volume II, No. 32) in the context of love's fears. Here it returns in the Vairāgyaśataka in its full existential form — applied to the ultimate fears: death, loss, dissolution. The same principle operates at every level: anticipatory anxiety is the real disease; when the feared thing actually arrives, the appropriate response is decisive engagement without flinching. The fearless person is not one who never feared — but one who acts decisively when fear arrives.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: भय न आल्यापर्यंत घाबरणं योग्य. पण भय आलं तेव्हा ते दिसलं की निर्भयपणे त्यावर घाव घालावा.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: हा श्लोक शृंगारशतकात होता (प्रेमाच्या भयाबद्दल), आता वैराग्यशतकात परत येतो — मोठ्या भयांसाठी: मृत्यू, हानी, विसर्जन. तोच नियम: येण्याआधी घाबरणं — पण आलं की सामोरं जा. निर्भय माणूस भयहीन नसतो — तो भय आलं की डगमगत नाही.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
जननी जन्मभूमिश्च स्वर्गादपि गरीयसी ।
इति रामायणे श्रुत्वा रामः किं नावबुध्यत ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Mātā yasya gṛhe nāsti bhāryā cāprikritopamā |
Araṇyaṃ tena gantavyaṃ yathāraṇyaṃ tathā gṛham ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: He whose house has no mother and whose wife is not of incomparable worth — for him the forest and the house are the same; he may as well go to the forest.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of domestic philosophy within the Vairāgyaśataka. The forest (araṇya) is the classical symbol of renunciation — withdrawal from home. But Bhartuhari says: for the person whose home lacks the warmth of a mother's presence and the virtue of a worthy wife, the home is already a forest. There is no difference between the two. The verse is not a prescription for renunciation but a definition of what makes a home: these two presences. Without them, it is already the forest.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: ज्याच्या घरी आई नाही, आणि ज्याची पत्नी अतुलनीय नाही — त्यासाठी वन आणि घर सारखंच. तो वनातच गेला तरी चालेल.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: घराची व्याख्या. आई आणि सत्पत्नी — या दोन असतील तर घर. नसतील तर घर वनासारखंच — एकाकी, उष्णतेशिवाय. भर्तृहरि वैराग्याच्या ठिकाणी हे सांगतो — घर-वन हा फरक मनात आहे, स्थानात नाही. जिथे प्रेम आणि साथ आहे तिथे घर, नाहीतर वनच.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
हे शम्भो शिव शङ्कर त्रिनयन त्रैलोक्यनाथ प्रभो
भूतेशाखिलभूतिभूषण हर व्योमोर्ध्वकेश प्रभो ।
सर्वज्ञ त्वमसीति वेद्मि सततं तत्किं न जानासि माम्
त्वत्पादे हृदयं ममास्ति सततं किं तत् न बोधस्यपि ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
He Śambho Śiva Śaṅkara trinayana trailokyanātha prabho
Bhūteśākhilabhūtibhūṣaṇa hara vyomordhvakeśa prabho |
Sarvajña tvamasīti vedmi satataṃ tatkiṃ na jānāsi māṃ
tvatpāde hṛdayaṃ mamāsti satataṃ kiṃ tan na bodhasyapi ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: O Śambhu, Śiva, Śaṅkara, three-eyed one, Lord of the three worlds; O Lord of all beings, adorned with all glories, remover of sorrow, sky-haired one; I always know that you are all-knowing — then do you not know me? My heart is always at your feet — do you not even perceive this?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The devotional culmination of the Vairāgyaśataka's penultimate section — a direct prayer to Śiva that is both supplication and gentle challenge. "You are all-knowing — then surely you know me? My heart is at your feet — do you not feel it?" The prayer moves from address (cataloguing Śiva's names and qualities) to intimate question. This is bhakti at its most direct: not petition but recognition, not distance but intimacy, a heart addressing its god as one who already knows.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: हे शंभो, शिव, शंकर, त्रिनयन, त्रैलोक्यनाथ; हे भूतेश, सर्वैश्वर्यभूषण, हर, व्योमकेश; तू सर्वज्ञ आहेस हे मला नेहमी माहीत आहे — मग तू मला का ओळखत नाहीस? माझं हृदय नेहमी तुझ्या पायी आहे — ते तुला जाणवत नाही का?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: शिवाची थेट प्रार्थना — पण त्यात एक गोड प्रश्न. "तू सर्वज्ञ आहेस — मग माझ्याबद्दल का माहीत नाही? माझं मन तुझ्याजवळ आहे — हे तुला दिसत नाही का?" हे भक्तीचं परम रूप — अंतर नाही, सलगी आहे. भर्तृहरिचं वैराग्य शेवटी देवाशी या जवळिकेत संपतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
एकेनापि सुपुत्रेण विद्यायुक्तेन साधुना ।
आह्लादितं कुलं सर्वं यथा चन्द्रेण शर्वरी ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Ekenāpi suputreṇa vidyāyuktena sāddhunā |
Āhlāditaṃ kulaṃ sarvaṃ yathā candreṇa śarvarī ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: By even one good son — learned and virtuous — the entire family is gladdened, just as the night is by the moon.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of gentle optimism about family and lineage. One person of genuine quality — learned and morally grounded — can illuminate an entire family just as a single moon illuminates the entire night. Bhartuhari does not require the whole family to be excellent; one such person is enough. The moon image is precise: there is only one moon, yet the night is not dark. The birth of one truly excellent person vindicates a whole generation.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: विद्यायुक्त आणि सज्जन असा एकाच सुपुत्राने संपूर्ण कुळ आनंदित होतं — जसं चंद्राने रात्र.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: रात्रीला चंद्र एकाच असतो — पण तो संपूर्ण रात्र उजळतो. एका खऱ्या, विद्वान आणि सज्जन व्यक्तीने संपूर्ण कुळाला प्रकाश मिळतो. अनेकांची गरज नाही — एक पुरे. भर्तृहरि येथे आशावादी आहे: कुळात एकच जरी चांगला असेल तर सगळं सार्थ होतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
किं कुलेन विशालेन विद्याहीनस्य देहिनः ।
दुर्जातिरपि विद्यावान् देवैरपि हि पूज्यते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kiṃ kulena viśālena vidyāhīnasya dehinaḥ |
Durjātirapi vidyāvān devairapi hi pūjyate ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: What is the use of a great family for one who has no learning? Even one born of low birth who has learning is honoured even by the gods.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A direct statement of meritocracy over birth. High birth without learning is worthless — a great lineage cannot substitute for the absence of genuine cultivation. And learning transcends birth entirely: even someone of low birth (durjāti) who possesses true knowledge is honoured by the gods themselves. Bhartuhari repeats this theme (as in No. 62, 77) because it evidently mattered deeply to him — the constant privileging of internal cultivation over external accident.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: विद्याहीन माणसाला मोठ्या कुळाचा काय उपयोग? नीच जन्माचाही विद्वान देवांनाही पूज्य असतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: मोठं घराणं आणि विद्या नाही — तर त्या घराण्याचा काय अर्थ? विद्या हीच खरी श्रेष्ठता. नीच जन्मातला विद्वानही देवांना वंदनीय. भर्तृहरि हे वारंवार सांगतो कारण त्याच्या काळात जन्माधारित श्रेष्ठतेचा दावा खूप मोठा होता. आणि आजही.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
अपूर्वः कोऽपि कल्याणी सम्प्रयोगस्तवानघे ।
भवत्यस्मिन् क्षणे भाव्यं यत् परं भवता सह ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Santāpastava saṃsarge saṃsargastava santāpe |
Dūre bhavatu samparkastava kiṃ tena me sukham ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Your company is pain; pain is in your company. Let your association be distant — what happiness do I have from it?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of renouncing the beloved — the Nītiśataka's counsel entering the domain of the Śṛṅgāraśataka's suffering. When association with someone — even a beloved — brings only pain, and pain brings only the desire for their company, Bhartuhari names it clearly: let that association be distant. This is not coldness but clarity — the recognising and naming of a toxic pattern. The verse could apply equally to a harmful friendship, a destructive passion, or any relationship where the connection itself causes what it was meant to cure.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: तुझ्या संगाने संताप; संतापात तुझी संगत. तुझी संगत दूर असो — त्यात माझं सुख काय?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: जेव्हा संगत स्वतःच दुःखाचं मूळ बनते — तेव्हा त्यापासून दूर जाणं शहाणपण. हे स्नेहाचा अभाव नाही — हे स्पष्टता आहे. ज्या नात्यात सोबत दुखवते आणि वियोग सुद्धा दुखवतो — त्यातून बाहेर पडणं हे वैराग्याची पायरी आहे. भर्तृहरि येथे व्यावहारिक आणि साफ बोलतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
स्वयं कृतानां पापानां फलं भुञ्जन्ति मानवाः ।
अतः पापाद्विनिवृत्तिः कर्तव्या बुद्धिमद्भिरिह ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Svayaṃ kṛtānāṃ pāpānāṃ phalaṃ bhuñjanti mānavāḥ |
Ataḥ pāpādvinirvṛttiḥ kartavyā buddhimadbhiriha ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Human beings experience the fruits of the wrongs they themselves have done. Therefore, the intelligent should here withdraw from wrong action.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of straightforward karmic ethics. The connection between action and consequence is presented not as divine punishment but as a natural order — one experiences the fruit of one's own acts. The prescription follows logically: the intelligent person therefore withdraws from wrong action. The verse does not require elaborate theology — simply the recognition that our actions return to us and the decision to act accordingly.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: मनुष्य स्वतः केलेल्या पापांचं फळ भोगतात. म्हणून बुद्धिमान माणसाने पापापासून दूर राहावे.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: कारण-परिणाम. स्वतः केलेलं भोगावं लागतं — देव शिक्षा देत नाही, कर्म फळ देतं. हे समजलं की पापाचं कारण नाही. भर्तृहरिचं नीतितत्त्व येथे साधं आहे: बुद्धिमान माणूस याचा विचार करतो आणि चुकीच्या मार्गापासून दूर राहतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
तावत् प्रतापो विजयश्च तावत्
तावत् प्रतिष्ठा नृपतेस्तु तावत् ।
संग्रामभूमौ न पलायते यत्
सत्त्वं हि युद्धे पुरुषस्य धर्मः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Tāvat pratāpo vijayaśca tāvat
Tāvat pratiṣṭhā nṛpatestu tāvat |
Saṃgrāmabhūmau na palāyate yat
sattvaṃ hi yuddhe puruṣasya dharmaḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: So long is the king's glory, victory, and honour — as long as he does not flee from the battlefield. Steadfastness in battle is the dharma of the person of courage.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of martial ethics within the Nītiśataka. The king's reputation is precisely co-extensive with his battlefield courage — it lasts as long as he does not run. Sattva (here meaning steadfastness, courage, the quality of not yielding) is the dharma of the courageous person. This is not glorification of war but a statement about character: in whatever field one has committed to, fleeing is dishonour and staying is the mark of genuine quality.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: राजाचा प्रताप, विजय आणि प्रतिष्ठा तोपर्यंत — जोपर्यंत तो युद्धभूमीतून पळत नाही. युद्धात स्थिर राहणं हाच शूर माणसाचा धर्म.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: पळणं म्हणजे सगळं गमावणं. राजाचा प्रताप, यश, मान — हे टिकतात जोपर्यंत तो उभा राहतो. पळाला की सगळं संपतं. भर्तृहरि येथे फक्त युद्धाबद्दल नाही बोलत — जे काम हाती घेतलं त्यात उभं राहण्याबद्दल बोलतो. जीवनातल्या कोणत्याही आव्हानात — पळणं म्हणजे हार.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
मूर्खो वदति विप्राणां नामगोत्रे पृच्छति ।
पण्डितो विद्वता जल्पेत् भाषां जानाति पण्डितः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Mūrkho vadati viprāṇāṃ nāmagoptre pṛcchati |
Paṇḍito vidvatā jalpeṭ bhāṣāṃ jānāti paṇḍitaḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The fool asks the name and lineage of the learned. The truly learned speaks through the quality of their learning — the scholar is known by their language.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about how knowledge reveals itself. The fool, meeting a learned person, asks for credentials — name, lineage, title. The genuinely learned person simply speaks — and their speech is their credential. The scholar is known by their language (bhāṣā — here meaning not just the language spoken but the quality, depth, and precision of expression). Credentials are the resort of those who cannot discern quality directly; the discerning person listens to how someone speaks and knows immediately.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: मूर्ख विप्रांचं नाव-गोत्र विचारतो. पंडित विद्वत्तेने बोलतो — पंडित भाषेने ओळखला जातो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: ज्ञान स्वतः बोलतं — प्रमाणपत्र नको. मूर्ख माणूस ओळखपत्र मागतो — नाव काय, गोत्र काय. पण खऱ्या विद्वानाचं ज्ञान त्याच्या बोलण्यातून दिसतं. शब्द, आवाज, तर्क — यातून समजतं कोण कुठे आहे. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: विद्वान ओळखायचा असेल तर फक्त ऐका.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
संगः सर्वात्मना त्याज्यो दोषवद्भिर्नरैः सदा ।
तेनैव महतां योगाद् याति पुण्यत्वमप्यधः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Saṃgaḥ sarvātmanā tyājyo doṣavadbhirnaraiḥ sadā |
Tenaiva mahatāṃ yogāt yāti puṇyatvamapyadhaḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Association with the faulty should always be given up entirely. Even by the company of the great, what is virtuous can go downward.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about the absolute need to give up bad association. The negative formulation is striking: even the company of the great can pull virtue downward if that "great" person is faulty. There are no exceptions — Bhartuhari says "sarvātmanā" (entirely, wholly) — not partial reduction but complete withdrawal. And even virtuous deeds (puṇya) can be undone by wrong association. The environment matters as much as the act.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: दोषी माणसांची संगत पूर्णपणे सोडावी. त्यांच्या योगाने मोठ्यांचे पुण्यही खाली जाते.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: "पूर्णपणे" — थोडी संगत नाही, थोडी चालेल असं नाही. भर्तृहरि स्पष्ट आहे: दोषी माणसांची संगत पूर्ण सोडा. कारण त्यांच्या योगाने मोठ्या माणसांचंही पुण्य क्षीण होतं. वाईट संगतीचा परिणाम — मग ती किती काळ का असेना — चांगल्या गोष्टींवर होतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
शक्यो वारयितुं जलेन हुतभुक् छत्रेण सूर्यातपो
नागेन्द्रो निशिताङ्कुशेन समदो दण्डेन गोगर्दभौ ।
व्याधिर्भेषजसंग्रहैश्च विविधैर्मन्त्रप्रयोगैर्विषं
सर्वस्यौषधमस्ति शास्त्रविहितं मूर्खस्य नास्त्यौषधम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Śakyo vārayituṃ jalena hutabhuk chatreṇa sūryātapo
Nāgendro niśitāṃkuśena samado daṇḍena gogardabhau |
Vyādhirbheṣajasaṃgrahaiśca vividhairmantraprayogairviṣaṃ
Sarvasyauṣadhamasti śāstraviihitaṃ mūrkhasyānastyauṣadhaṃ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Fire can be checked by water; the sun's heat by an umbrella; a rogue elephant by a sharp goad; cattle and donkeys by a stick; disease by collections of medicines; poison by various mantra applications — there is a scriptural remedy for everything. For the fool there is no remedy.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The great catalogue of remedies — and the single exception.
