Every destructive force in nature has its antidote: water for fire, shade for sun, goad for elephant, stick for animals, medicine for disease, mantra for poison. But the fool? No remedy exists. The verse is the culmination of the Nītiśataka's repeated observations about the incorrigible fool — the person who cannot be reasoned with, instructed, or cured. The world has provided solutions for every problem except this one.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: अग्नी पाण्याने, सूर्यताप छत्राने, मत्त हत्ती अंकुशाने, गाय-गाढव काठीने, रोग औषधाने, विष मंत्रप्रयोगाने वारता येतो. प्रत्येक गोष्टीसाठी शास्त्राने उपाय आहे. मूर्खाला उपाय नाही.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: सगळ्यांचं औषध आहे — अग्नी, सूर्य, हत्ती, रोग, विष. पण मूर्खाचं? — नाही. हे नीतिशतकातले सर्वात धारदार विधान. जगातल्या प्रत्येक समस्येला उत्तर आहे, एकाशिवाय — हट्टी, अज्ञानी माणूस. भर्तृहरि येथे थांबतो — अधिक काही बोलण्याची गरज नाही.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
काव्येषु नाटकं रम्यं तत्र रम्या शकुन्तला ।
तत्रापि च चतुर्थोऽङ्कस्तत्र श्लोकचतुष्टयम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kāvyeṣu nāṭakaṃ ramyaṃ tatra ramyā śakuntalā |
Tatrāpi ca caturtho'ṅkastatra ślokacatuṣṭayam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Among literary works, drama is the most delightful; among dramas, Śakuntalā is the most beautiful; within it, the fourth act is the most moving; within that, four particular verses.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: Bhartuhari's famous literary criticism in miniature — a cascade of superlatives. From all literature: drama. From drama: Kālidāsa's Abhijñānaśākuntalam. From that: Act IV (the separation of Śakuntalā from the hermitage — widely considered the most emotionally powerful section of any Sanskrit play). From that: four specific verses. This exercise in critical precision is itself an act of literary taste — identifying the finest thing within the finest thing within the finest thing.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: काव्यांमध्ये नाटक सुंदर; त्यात शाकुंतल सर्वोत्कृष्ट; त्यातही चौथा अंक; त्यातही चार श्लोक.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: भर्तृहरिची साहित्यसमीक्षा — उत्तरोत्तर श्रेष्ठांचं शोधणं. सगळ्या साहित्यात नाटक, त्यात शाकुंतल, त्यात चौथा अंक (शकुंतलेचा निरोप — सर्वात हृदयद्रावक), त्यातही चार श्लोक. हे रसिकतेचं सर्वोच्च रूप आहे — सर्वोत्तमात सर्वोत्तम शोधण्याचं कौशल्य.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
वाचामेतानि चत्वारि रूपाणि भुवि भारत ।
सत्यं प्रियं च हितं च चतुर्थमनुशासनम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Vācāmetāni catvāri rūpāṇi bhuvi bhārata |
Satyaṃ priyaṃ ca hitaṃ ca caturthamanusāsanaṃ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Speech has these four forms on earth: truth, pleasant speech, beneficial speech, and as a fourth — instruction.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of rhetorical taxonomy. The four forms of speech are: satya (true), priya (pleasant), hita (beneficial), and anusāsana (instruction, correction). The ideal speech combines all four — but in practice they can conflict: truth may not be pleasant; what is pleasant may not be beneficial; instruction may be unwelcome. Bhartuhari does not rank them but names them as the four regions within which all speech operates. The wise speaker navigates all four with awareness.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: वाणीचे जगात चार रूपे आहेत: सत्य, प्रिय, हित, आणि चौथे अनुशासन.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: वाणीचे चार प्रकार. सत्य — खरं. प्रिय — गोड. हित — फायदेशीर. अनुशासन — शिकवणारं, सुधारणारं. आदर्श वाणी या चारांना एकत्र आणते — पण ते नेहमी शक्य नसतं. सत्य गोड नसतं; गोड हितकर नसतं. शहाण्या माणसाला हे चारही जाणून बोलणं येतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
पर्जन्यो वसुधायां च समः सर्वत्र वर्षति ।
विशेषस्तत्र भूमेः स्यात् कुशला यत्र वर्धते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Parjanyo vasudhāyāṃ ca samaḥ sarvatra varṣati |
Viśeṣastatra bhūmeḥ syāt kuśalā yatra vardhate ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Rain falls equally on all the earth; the distinction is in the ground — where the skilled grows.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about the equality of opportunity and the inequality of cultivation. The rain is democratic — it falls on fertile soil and barren rock alike. The difference lies not in the rain but in the ground that receives it. Knowledge, wisdom, teaching — these rain down with some equality on those who are present. The distinction is in the individual's inner ground: the prepared mind, the cultivated character, the fertile attention that allows the rain of teaching to produce growth.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: पाऊस सगळ्या पृथ्वीवर सारखाच पडतो; फरक त्या जमिनीत, जिथे कुशल वाढतं.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: पाऊस समान — पण परिणाम वेगळे. सुपीक जमिनीत वाढतं, नापीक जमिनीत नाही. ज्ञान, शिक्षण, संधी — हे सगळ्यांना सारखेच मिळतात. फरक आतल्या तयारीत — मन तयार आहे का, चारित्र्य सुपीक आहे का. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: संधी देणं आपल्या हाती नाही, पण जमीन सुपीक करणं आपल्या हाती आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
दृष्टिपूतं न्यसेत् पादं वस्त्रपूतं जलं पिबेत् ।
शास्त्रपूतं वदेद्वाक्यं मनःपूतं समाचरेत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyaset pādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pibet |
Śāstrapūtaṃ vadetvākyaṃ manaḥpūtaṃ samācaret ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Place the foot after purifying with the eye; drink water after straining through cloth; speak words purified by scripture; act after purifying through the mind.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of four-level purification practice. Each act has its corresponding purifying instrument: the eye for the foot's placement (look before you step), cloth for water (filter before drinking), scripture for speech (consider whether your words accord with wisdom before speaking), and the mind for action (examine your conscience before acting). The verse is a prescription for mindfulness at every level — physical, verbal, and mental — moving from the most basic to the most interior.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: डोळ्यांनी पाहून पाऊल टाका; कापडाने गाळून पाणी प्या; शास्त्राने शुद्ध करून वाक्य बोला; मनाने शुद्ध करून आचरण करा.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: चार स्तरांवर शुद्धता. पाऊल — डोळे पाहतात. पाणी — कापड गाळतं. शब्द — शास्त्र तपासतं. कृती — मन तपासतं. साधं ते गहन — शरीर ते मन. प्रत्येक कृतीला त्याचं शुद्धीकरण. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: सावधानता ही एक संस्कृती आहे — प्रत्येक स्तरावर.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
न गृहं गृहमित्याहुः गृहिणी गृहमुच्यते ।
गृहं तु गृहिणीहीनं कान्तारमतिरिच्यते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Na gṛhaṃ gṛhamityāhur gṛhiṇī gṛhamucyate |
Gṛhaṃ tu gṛhiṇīhīnaṃ kāntāramatirīcyate ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: They do not call the house "home" — the householder-woman is called the home. A house without a householder-woman surpasses even a wilderness in its desolation.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of profound domestic philosophy. The physical structure — walls, roof, rooms — is not the home. The home is constituted by the gṛhiṇī — the woman who inhabits and animates it. Without her, the house is worse than a wilderness: a wilderness has its own life, its trees and birds; a house without its animating presence is a hollow shell, more desolate than empty forest. This is Bhartuhari's tribute to the woman as the maker of home.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: घर म्हणजे घर असं म्हणत नाहीत — गृहिणीलाच घर म्हणतात. गृहिणीशिवाय घर अरण्यापेक्षाही जड.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: घर म्हणजे भिंती नाहीत — घर म्हणजे गृहिणी. ती असेल तर घर; नसेल तर अरण्यापेक्षाही उजाड. कारण अरण्याला स्वतःचं जीवन असतं — रिकाम्या घराला नाही. भर्तृहरिचं गृहिणीबद्दलचं हे वर्णन गहन आहे: ती घराचं प्राण आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
नास्ति मेघसमं तोयं नास्ति चात्मसमं बलम् ।
नास्ति चक्षुः समं तेजो नास्ति धान्यसमं प्रियम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Nāsti meghasamaṃ toyaṃ nāsti cātmasamaṃ balam |
Nāsti cakṣuḥsamaṃ tejo nāsti dhānyasamaṃ priyam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: There is no water like rainwater; no strength like the strength of the self; no radiance like that of the eye; no dear thing like grain.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: Four comparative statements about the highest of each kind. Rainwater is the purest, most life-giving water. The strength of the self (ātmaśakti — one's own inner power) surpasses all external strength. The radiance of the eye is the finest light — because it sees. And grain is the most dear of all things because it sustains life. The verse values the simple, the essential, the inherent — over the elaborate, the acquired, the external.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: मेघाच्या पाण्यासारखं पाणी नाही; आत्मशक्तीसारखं बळ नाही; डोळ्यांच्या तेजासारखं तेज नाही; धान्यासारखं प्रिय नाही.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: चार सर्वोच्च — पाण्यात, बळात, तेजात, आणि प्रियात. पावसाचं पाणी शुद्धतम. आत्मशक्ती सर्वात मोठी — कारण ती स्वतःची. डोळ्यांचं तेज सर्वोत्तम — कारण ते पाहतं. धान्य सर्वात प्रिय — कारण ते जगवतं. भर्तृहरि साध्या, मूलभूत, स्वतःच्या गोष्टींना श्रेष्ठत्व देतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
विद्वान् प्रशस्यते लोके विद्वान् गच्छति गौरवम् ।
विद्यया लभते सर्वं विद्या सर्वत्र पूज्यते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Vidvān praśasyate loke vidvān gacchati gauravāṃ |
Vidyayā labhate sarvaṃ vidyā sarvatra pūjyate ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The learned person is praised in the world; the learned person attains honour; through knowledge one obtains everything; knowledge is revered everywhere.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The Nītiśataka's concluding affirmation of vidyā. The verse has a quality of summing up — four statements about the learned person and knowledge, each one a slight variation on the same theme, building through repetition into a final chord. Learning brings praise, honour, all things, and universal reverence. This is Bhartuhari's final word from the Nītiśataka: after all the warnings, the irony, the social observation — the thing to pursue above all is knowledge.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: विद्वान जगात प्रशंसित; विद्वानाला मान मिळतो; विद्येने सगळं मिळतं; विद्या सर्वत्र पूजली जाते.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: नीतिशतकाचा समारोप. विद्वान — प्रशंसित, मानित. विद्या — सगळं देते, सर्वत्र पूजिली जाते. भर्तृहरिने शंभर श्लोकांत माणसाचे स्वभाव, समाज, नाती, धोके, गुण — सगळं सांगितलं. आणि शेवटी एकच संदेश: विद्या मिळवा — हाच मार्ग, हाच आधार.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणाः यदि वा स्तुवन्तु
लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् ।
अद्यैव मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा
न्याय्यात् पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Nindantu nītinipuṇāḥ yadi vā stuvanttu
Lakṣmīḥ samāviśatu gacchatu vā yatheṣṭam |
Adyaiva maraṇamastu yugāntare vā
nyāyyāt pathaḥ pravicalanti padaṃ na dhīrāḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Let the wise praise or condemn; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or in another age — the steadfast never waver from the path of righteousness by even a single step.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: This verse appeared earlier (Volume II, No. 33) — Bhartuhari returns to it here as the Śṛṅgāraśataka approaches its close because it functions as a kind of moral spine running through all three śatakas. Having explored desire, love, beauty, and longing in all their complexity, the śataka returns to this bedrock: no circumstance — praise, blame, wealth, poverty, death itself — justifies deviation from the path of justice. The dhīra (steadfast person) is the answer to all three śatakas.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: नीतिज्ञ निंदा करोत वा स्तुती; लक्ष्मी येवो वा जावो; आजच मृत्यू येवो वा युगानंतर — धीर माणसे न्यायाच्या मार्गावरून एक पाऊलही मागे येत नाहीत.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: हा श्लोक आधी आला होता — पण तो इथे परत येतो कारण शृंगारशतकाचा समारोप या सत्यावर होणं योग्य आहे. प्रेम, सौंदर्य, इच्छा, विरह — या सगळ्यातून गेल्यावर भर्तृहरि म्हणतो: शेवटी धीर माणूस न्यायाच्या मार्गावर उभा राहतो. कोणत्याही परिस्थितीत.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
रत्यर्थं भुवनत्रयस्य विधिना निर्माय रूपं परं
सौन्दर्यामृतवारिराशिनिधिना लावण्यलक्ष्म्या च ।
प्रीत्यर्थं यदि देवताः प्रणमितुं देवेन्द्रमाप्यागतं
नान्यः कोऽपि विशेषणं विरहितो देव्याः प्रभावो महान् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Ratyarthaṃ bhuvanatrayasya vidhinā nirmāya rūpaṃ paraṃ
Saundaryāmṛtavāriranidhinā lāvaṇyalakṣmyā ca |
Prītyarthaṃ yadi devatāḥ praṇamituṃ devendramāpyāgataṃ
nānyaḥ ko'pi viśeṣaṇaṃ virahito devyāḥ prabhāvo mahān ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The creator made the supreme form for the delight of the three worlds; with the ocean of the nectar of beauty and the grace of loveliness. If even the gods come to bow before Indra for joy — there is no other description: the power of the Goddess is great, without attribute.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of theological eroticism — the Goddess's beauty is so supreme that even Indra, king of gods, bows before it. The creator made the supreme beautiful form (the beloved's, the Goddess's — they merge here) as the delight of all three worlds. Beauty is not merely human and temporal; it is cosmic and divine. The "power of the Goddess" (devyāḥ prabhāva) that transcends all description is Bhartuhari's closing vision of the Śṛṅgāraśataka's subject: beauty is ultimately divine.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: विधात्याने तिन्ही जगांच्या आनंदासाठी सर्वोच्च रूप बनवलं — सौंदर्यामृताच्या समुद्राने आणि लावण्यलक्ष्मीने. देव आनंदासाठी इंद्रालाही नमायला आले — तर दुसरं काय वर्णन? देवीचा प्रभाव महान, वर्णनातीत.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: सौंदर्य दैवी आहे. तीन जगांच्या आनंदासाठी विधात्याने हे रूप निर्माण केलं. इंद्रही नमतो. देवीचा प्रभाव शब्दांपलीकडे. भर्तृहरि शृंगारशतकाच्या शेवटी सांगतो: प्रेमाची आराधना केली — पण शेवटी सौंदर्य दैवी आहे. आणि दैवाला नमस्कार.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
नोद्विजेत तनुं त्यक्त्वा मनसा मनसां गतः ।
रूपं बन्धकरं नास्ति मनसो नास्ति संशयः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Mugdhāyāḥ prathamāvalokanasukhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ yasya tad
vaktum ko'pi na śaknoti na vivekī lajjate |
Utkaṇṭhāvaśavartinā manasā rātriṃ viyuktaḥ kṛtaṃ
jīvāmi kva va yāsyato bata kim āsthā jīvite'sminnapi ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The joy of a first sight of the innocent one is ordinary to whoever has it — no one can speak it; the discerning person is not ashamed. With a mind at the mercy of yearning, separated through the night — "I am alive; where will I go? — what is the point of this very life?"
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of complete erotic desolation. The first sight of the beloved is so wonderful that it cannot be articulated — but this is a commonplace joy, shared by many. What cannot be shared or spoken is the anguish of the night of separation, when the mind is entirely at yearning's mercy. The final question — "what is the point of this life?" — is not suicidal despair but the lover's genuine philosophical bewilderment: existence without the beloved seems pointless.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: भोळ्या प्रियेचं पहिलं दर्शन-सुख साधारण असतं — कोणी सांगू शकत नाही; विवेकी लाजत नाही. उत्कंठेच्या आहारी गेलेल्या मनाने रात्र वियोगात घालवली — "मी जगतो; कुठे जाईन? या जगण्यात अर्थ काय?"
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: पहिलं दर्शन सांगता येत नाही — ते बोलण्यापलीकडे. आणि मग रात्रभर विरह — मन उत्कंठेत. "जगतो; कुठे जाऊ?" हा प्रश्न म्हणजे निराशा नाही — ती भोवळ आहे. ती व्यक्ती नसेल तर जगण्याचा अर्थ काय? भर्तृहरि हे प्रेमाच्या गहनतेचं वर्णन आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
पद्मानां सौरभं गृह्णन् पद्मिन्यस्ताः प्रयान्ति हि ।
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि यतः संग उपायते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Āśleṣasukhāni yāni mukhasudhāpānāni yāni priye
Madhurāṇi ca bhāṣitāni tava yāni smitāni ca |
Smaraṃstāni sadā vivṛttamanasā rātrau viyukte mayi
svapne'bhyadhikaṃ ca dṛṣṭam iti me citrā gatirdaivataḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The joys of embracing; the drinking of the nectar of your face, O beloved; your sweet words; your smiles — always remembering these with a turned-away mind, separated at night, I have seen them more intensely in dreams. How strange is the path of fate for me.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of dream-intensified memory. The lover, separated, remembers the beloved's embrace, the nectar of her lips, her sweet words, her smiles. But the remarkable turn: in dreams, these remembered pleasures are experienced more intensely (abhyadhikaṃ) than in waking life. The dream exceeds the reality it recalls. "How strange is the path of fate" — not bitterness but wonder at the paradox: the absent beloved is more present in dream than the present one was in waking.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: आलिंगनाचे सुख, हे प्रिये, तुझ्या मुखाचं अमृत पिणं, तुझे गोड शब्द, तुझं हास्य — वियोगाच्या रात्री हटलेल्या मनाने नेहमी आठवताना — स्वप्नात ते अधिकच तीव्रतेने दिसतं. दैवाची माझ्यासाठी विचित्र गती.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: स्वप्नात वास्तवापेक्षा अधिक. आलिंगन, मुखसुधा, शब्द, हास्य — हे जागेपणी होतं. पण स्वप्नात ते अधिकच तीव्र. हे विरोधाभास आहे — आणि भर्तृहरि त्याला "दैवाची विचित्र गती" म्हणतो. नशीब विचित्र आहे: जे गेलं ते स्वप्नात जास्त जवळ येतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
वियोगिनां हृदये वह्निर्विरहाख्यो ज्वलत्यदः ।
भस्मकुर्वन् शरीरं यः सागरस्यापि दूरतः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Viyogināṃ hṛdaye vahnirvvirahākhyo jvalatyardaḥ |
Bhasmakurvan śarīraṃ yaḥ sāgarasyāpi dūrataḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: In the hearts of those separated, the fire named Viraha burns — reducing the body to ash, far beyond even the ocean's power to extinguish.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of extreme hyperbole — which is to say, a verse that means exactly what it says. The fire of viraha (separation) burns within the heart and consumes the body. The ocean — capable of extinguishing any ordinary fire — cannot reach this fire because it burns inside. External remedies are useless against internal fire. This is the Śṛṅgāraśataka's sharpest image of the completeness of love's suffering: it is beyond reach of any cooling force.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: विरहींच्या हृदयात विरहनामक अग्नी जळतो — शरीर भस्म करत; समुद्रालाही विझवता येत नाही.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: विरहाचा अग्नी आतला आहे — समुद्र बाहेरून विझवतो, पण आत काय पोहोचेल? शरीर भस्म होतं पण अग्नी विझत नाही. भर्तृहरिची ही अतिशयोक्ती सत्य आहे — विरहाची आग खरोखरच अशी असते. बाहेरचं काहीही ती शांत करू शकत नाही.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
साहसे श्रीः प्रतिवसति साहसे मित्रसंचयः ।
साहसे सर्वमाप्नोति तस्मात् साहसिको भव ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Sāhase śrīḥ prativasati sāhase mitrasaṃcayaḥ |
Sāhase sarvamāpnoti tasmāt sāhasiko bhava ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Prosperity dwells in boldness; a collection of friends dwells in boldness; everything is obtained through boldness. Therefore, be bold.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of pure encouragement within the Śṛṅgāraśataka — applicable equally to love, to enterprise, and to life. Prosperity, friendship, and everything desirable are said to inhabit boldness (sāhasa). The conclusion is direct: therefore, be bold. In the context of the Śṛṅgāraśataka, sāhasa in love is the courage to declare, to approach, to commit — the timid lover gets nothing. In life more broadly, the principle holds: the cautious may preserve what they have; only the bold can gain what they do not.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: साहसात श्री राहते; साहसात मित्रांची जमवाजमव; साहसाने सगळं मिळतं. म्हणून साहसी हो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: साहसात राहते लक्ष्मी, मित्र, सगळं. भर्तृहरि येथे शृंगारात सांगतो: प्रेमात साहस नसेल तर काय? समोर जाऊन बोलणं, स्वतःला उघड करणं — हे साहस. आयुष्यातही — फक्त जपणारे नाही मिळवत, साहसी मिळवतात. तर साहसी हो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
पन्थानं ते गन्तुमिच्छामि दूरं
तत्र स्थित्वा त्वत्प्रसादेन देवि ।
शान्तिं यास्यामि किमिति वदेत् पथिकस्त्वत्समागमे
वसन् पुण्यस्त्वामेव गायतीति ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Panthānaṃ te gantumicchāmi dūraṃ
tatra sthitvā tvatprasādena devi |
Śāntiṃ yāsyāmi kimiti vadet pathikastvat-samāgame
vasan puṇyastvāmeva gāyatīti ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: "I wish to travel your road, O Goddess, far away — dwelling there by your grace, I will attain peace." What would the traveller say upon meeting you? The virtuous one dwelling in your company sings only of you.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A devotional verse within the erotic śataka — the beloved transformed again into the Goddess, the journey of love becoming a spiritual path. The traveller seeks peace at the end of the road by the Goddess's grace. And the virtuous one who dwells in her company has only one song: her. This is the convergence of bhakti and śṛṅgāra — the beloved and the divine are one, and to be in the presence of either is to sing of nothing else.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: "हे देवी, तुझ्या मार्गावर दूर जाण्याची इच्छा आहे — तिथे राहून तुझ्या प्रसादाने शांती मिळेल." वाटसरू तुझ्या भेटीत काय म्हणेल? — तुझ्या सहवासात राहणारा पुण्यवान फक्त तुझ्याच गाण्याने गातो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: प्रिया पुन्हा देवी बनते, प्रेमाचा मार्ग आध्यात्मिक प्रवास बनतो. देवीच्या प्रसादाने शांती. आणि जो तिच्यासोबत राहतो, तो फक्त तिचंच गातो — दुसरं काही नाही. भर्तृहरिचे शृंगार आणि भक्ती इथे एकत्र येतात. प्रेम आणि ईश्वर वेगळे नाहीत.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
क्षणं बाला क्षणं युवती क्षणं वृद्धा च रूपिणी ।
यथा चन्द्रकला लीला नाटयते जगतां दृशि ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kṣaṇaṃ bālā kṣaṇaṃ yuvatī kṣaṇaṃ vṛddhā ca rūpiṇī |
Yathā candrakalā līlā nāṭayate jagatāṃ dṛśi ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: For a moment a child, for a moment a young woman, for a moment an old woman — the beautiful one plays her role before the eyes of the world like the phases of the moon.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse that presents the entire arc of a woman's life — and by extension, the human life — as the phases of the moon. The moon does not lose anything as it waxes and wanes; it plays through its phases as a single continuous performance. The beautiful one's life from child to elder is similarly a single lunar performance — all phases are the same moon, all stages are the same person. The verb nāṭayate (acts out, plays) gives the image a theatrical warmth.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: क्षण बालपण, क्षण तारुण्य, क्षण वृद्धापकाळ — रूपवान स्त्री चंद्राच्या कलांसारखी जगाच्या नजरेसमोर लीला करते.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: चंद्राच्या कला — एकाच चंद्राचे वेगवेगळे रूप. बालपण, तारुण्य, वृद्धत्व — एकाच माणसाचे टप्पे. चंद्र प्रत्येक कलेत तोच असतो — माणूसही. "लीला" — हे खेळणं आहे, हरवणं नाही. भर्तृहरि जीवनाच्या टप्प्यांना दुःखाने नाही, चंद्राच्या सौंदर्याने बघतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
वित्तं बन्धुर्वयः कर्म विद्या भवति पञ्चमी ।
एतानि माननीयानि राजभ्यो बहुमानितात् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Vitttaṃ bandhurvayaḥ karma vidyā bhavati pañcamī |
Etāni mānanīyāni rājabdhyo bahumānitāt ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Wealth, kinship, age, deed, and learning as the fifth — these are to be honoured, in ascending order from the respect paid by kings.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A taxonomy of honour in descending order from the worldly to the spiritual. Kings honour wealth; above wealth is family connection (social belonging); above that is age (experience); above that is deed (what one has actually done); and above all is vidyā — knowledge. This ranking implicitly critiques the order in which the world actually operates: wealth comes first in the world's eye, but learning is the highest. The verse sets the corrected hierarchy.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: धन, बंधू, वय, कर्म, आणि पाचवी विद्या — हे सन्माननीय आहेत, राजाकडून मिळणाऱ्या बहुमानापेक्षा चढत्या क्रमाने.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: पाच गुणांचा चढता क्रम. जगात राजा धनाला आधी मान देतो. त्याच्यावर बंधुत्व, त्यावर वय, त्यावर कर्म. आणि सर्वोच्च — विद्या. भर्तृहरि जगाचा क्रम आणि खरा क्रम यांची तुलना करतो. जगात धन आधी — पण खऱ्या अर्थाने विद्या सर्वोच्च.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
यां चिन्तयामि सततं मयि सा विरक्ता
साप्यन्यमिच्छति जनं स जनोऽन्यसक्तः ।
अस्मत्कृते च परिशुष्यति काचिदन्या
धिक् तां च तं च मदनं च इमां च मां च ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Yāṃ cintayāmi satataṃ mayi sā viraktā
sāpyanyamicchati janaṃ sa jano'nyasakttaḥ |
Asmatkṛte ca pariśuṣyati kācidanyā
dhik tāṃ ca taṃ ca madanaṃ ca imāṃ ca māṃ ca ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: She I constantly think of is indifferent to me; she desires another man; that man is attached to someone else; and for my sake, some other woman withers away. Curse on her, and on him, and on Kāma, and on that other woman, and on me.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: Perhaps the most darkly comic verse in all three śatakas. Bhartuhari maps out a five-person chain of unrequited desire: the poet loves A, A loves B, B loves C, D loves the poet. And none of these desires meet their object. The final "curse on all of us" — including the speaker himself — is both funny and devastating. It is the śataka's most honest moment about desire's structural absurdity: the entire arrangement is designed to produce maximum frustration.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: जिला मी सतत आठवतो, ती माझ्याबद्दल उदासीन; तीही दुसऱ्याला इच्छिते; तो दुसऱ्याशी अनुरक्त; आणि माझ्यासाठी एखादी अन्य कोमेजते. धिक्कार तिला, त्याला, कामाला, त्या दुसरीला, आणि मलाही!
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: इच्छेची साखळी — कोणीही कोणाला मिळत नाही. मी तिला, ती त्याला, तो दुसऱ्याला — आणि माझ्यासाठी एखादी जळते. हे विनोदी आहे — पण त्यात विदारक सत्य आहे. काम असंच काम करतो — अव्यवस्थित, आंधळा, सगळ्यांना दुखवतो. "धिक्कार सगळ्यांना — आणि मलाही!" — हे प्रामाणिक आत्मविलोकन आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
कर्तव्यं तदिदं हि मानवसुखं रात्रेर्दिनस्यान्तरे
तुच्छं तुच्छतरं च सर्वमपरं शश्वद्विलासात्परम् ।
आयुःपर्यवसानपर्यवसितं प्रेम्णश्च सत्यत्वतः
संभोगोत्सुकमानसं नु किमिदं भोगेन तृप्तिं व्रजेत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kartavyaṃ tadidaṃ hi mānavasukhaṃ rātrerdinasyāntare
tucchaṃ tucchatataraṃ ca sarvamparaṃ śaśvadvilāsātparam |
Āyuḥparyavasānaparyavasitaṃ premṇaśca satyatvataḥ
saṃbhogotsukamanasaṃ nu kimidaṃ bhogena tṛptiṃ vrajet ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: This — the happiness of human beings, between night and day — is the thing to be done. Everything else is trivial, more trivial still, beyond the eternal play of love. Ending at life's end, and from love's truth — can a mind eager for enjoyment ever find satisfaction through enjoyment?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of philosophical questioning about the nature of enjoyment. Human happiness exists between the stretches of night and day — in the waking, active, loving hours. Everything else is diminished by comparison. And yet the final question is the most honest: can a mind hungry for enjoyment (saṃbhogotsukamanasaṃ) ever find genuine satisfaction through enjoyment itself? The śṛṅgāra's implicit answer: no. Which is why the śataka moves toward vairāgya.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: रात्र आणि दिवसाच्या मध्ये मानवी सुख हेच करण्याचं. बाकी सगळं क्षुल्लक, अधिकच क्षुल्लक, प्रेमाच्या विलासापलीकडे. आयुष्याच्या अंतावर संपणारं, प्रेमाच्या सत्यतेने — भोगासाठी आसुसलेलं मन भोगाने तृप्त होऊ शकतं का?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: शेवटचा प्रश्न: भोगाने भोगाची तहान भागते का? शृंगारशतकाचं उत्तर: नाही. म्हणूनच पुढे वैराग्य. भर्तृहरि प्रेमाचं मूल्य नाकारत नाही — पण सांगतो: भोगात तृप्ती नाही. त्यापलीकडे जायला हवं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
या कुन्देन्दुतुषारहारधवला या शुभ्रवस्त्रावृता
या वीणावरदण्डमण्डितकरा या श्वेतपद्मासना ।
या ब्रह्माच्युतशंकरप्रभृतिभिर्देवैः सदा पूजिता
सा मां पातु सरस्वती भगवती निःशेषजाड्यापहा ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Yā kundendutuṣārahāradhavalā yā śubhravāstrāvṛtā
Yā vīṇāvaradaṇḍamaṇḍitakarā yā śvetapadmāsanā |
Yā brahmācyutaśaṃkaraprabhṛtibhirdevaiḥ sadā pūjitā
Sā māṃ pātu sarasvatī bhagavatī niḥśeṣajāḍyāpahā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: She who is white as jasmine-blossom, moon, and snow-garland; clothed in pure white garments; whose hands are adorned with the vīṇā and the rod of boons; who is seated on a white lotus; who is always worshipped by Brahma, Viṣṇu, Śiva and the other gods — may that Goddess Saraswatī, remover of all dullness, protect me.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: This verse opened the Śṛṅgāraśataka (No. 20, Volume I). It returns here as the Śṛṅgāraśataka approaches its close — Bhartuhari framing his erotic poetry within an invocation to the goddess of learning. The śataka that began with a prayer to clarity and knowledge ends by returning to that prayer. All the beauty, desire, and longing of the Śṛṅgāraśataka is held within this white frame of divine intelligence.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: कुंद, चंद्र, हिमहारासारखी धवल; शुभ्रवस्त्र; हातात वीणा आणि वरदंड; श्वेत कमळासनावर; ब्रह्मा-विष्णू-शंकरांनी सदा पूजिलेली — ती भगवती सरस्वती, सर्व जडत्व दूर करणारी, माझं रक्षण करो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: शृंगारशतक सरस्वतीने सुरू झालं होतं — सरस्वतीनेच संपतं. हे वर्तुळ पूर्ण होतं. प्रेम, सौंदर्य, इच्छा, विरह — या सगळ्यावर विद्येची देवी प्रकाश टाकते. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: शृंगार ज्ञानाशिवाय पूर्ण नाही. सुरुवात आणि शेवट — एकच.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
देहो देवालयः प्रोक्तो जीवो देवः सनातनः ।
त्यजेदज्ञाननिर्माल्यं सोऽहं भावेन पूजयेत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Mugdhe śubhrāṃ tanumurasi mā kuru mañjīracandanaṃ
candre dṛṣṭe'pi madanamapi nāśayati sphuṭam |
Śrotrāṃ smitaṃ śubhramapi saudhataṭe sthitāyāḥ
premṇā pūrṇā hṛdayamapi karoti vicetanam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: O innocent one, do not apply sandal paste and anklets to your fair body — even in the presence of the moon, it clearly destroys desire. Even a clear smile on the hearing, standing on the mansion's terrace — one whose heart is full of love becomes overwhelmed.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of playful erotic counsel — the lover addressing the beloved and paradoxically asking her not to adorn herself, because her natural beauty without ornament is more overwhelming than her adorned presence. The moon itself destroys desire by comparison — but the simple smile of the woman whose heart is full of love renders even the steadfast person overwhelmed. Unadorned natural beauty exceeds all ornament.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: हे भोळ्या, तुझ्या शुभ्र अंगावर चंदन आणि पैंजण लावू नकोस — चंद्र दिसल्यावरही तो मदन नाश करतो. उंच छतावर उभ्या राहिलेल्या तुझं स्पष्ट हास्य ऐकताना — प्रेमाने भरलेलं हृदय मोहित होतं.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: सजल्याशिवाय अधिक सुंदर. चंदन-पैंजण नको — तुझी नैसर्गिक सुंदरता पुरे. चंद्र दिसला तरी विचलित होतो — पण तुझं हास्य? — प्रेमाने भरलेलं मन कोलमडतं. भर्तृहरि येथे नैसर्गिक सौंदर्याला कृत्रिम सजावटीपेक्षा वरचं ठेवतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
कदाचिल्लीलया भर्तुः पादन्यासानुकारिणी ।
स्वयमेव स्थिता बाला प्रिया प्रियतमस्य सा ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kadācillīlayā bhartuḥ pādanyāsānukāriṇī |
Svayameva sthitā bālā priyā priyatamasya sā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Sometimes playfully imitating the footsteps of her husband's gait, standing by herself — she is the beloved of the most beloved.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of extraordinary domestic intimacy. The young wife, alone, playfully imitates the way her husband walks — his gait, his pace, his footstep placement. She is by herself; this is not a performance for anyone. The verse captures a private moment of love that is beyond longing or declaration — it is love as embodied imitation, as the beloved becoming the beloved through play. This is perhaps the most tender image in the entire Śṛṅgāraśataka.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: कधीकधी खेळत खेळत पतीच्या पावलांचं अनुकरण करणारी, एकटी उभी असलेली ती — ती प्रियतमाची सर्वात प्रिया आहे.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: एकटी असताना पतीच्या पावलांचं अनुकरण. हे कोणासाठी नाही — ती स्वतःसाठी करते, खेळत खेळत. प्रेमाचं हे रूप शब्दांपलीकडचं आहे. आत्मसात झालेलं प्रेम — जे एकांतातही जगतं. भर्तृहरिचं हे चित्र शृंगारशतकातलं सर्वात हळुवार आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
प्रेम्णः किंचिदभीष्टमाह मदनः किंचिद् व्रियते प्रिया
किंचिच्च स्वयमेव नेत्रचपलः कुर्यात् स्वसङ्कल्पतः ।
एतस्मिन् क्षणे चेतनं हृदि मम प्रेमाम्बुधेः सङ्गमे
जानीहि त्वमपि प्रिये विरहिणां वार्तां विना दूतिका ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Premṇaḥ kiṃcidabhīṣṭamāha madanaḥ kiṃcid vriyate priyā
kiṃcicca svayameva netracapalaḥ kuryāt svasaṃkalpataḥ |
Etasmin kṣaṇe cetanaṃ hṛdi mama premāmbudheḥ saṃgame
jānīhi tvamapi priye virāhiṇāṃ vārtāṃ vinā dūtikā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Some of love's desire is spoken by Kāma; some is chosen by the beloved; some the restless eye does on its own by decision. In this moment of the ocean of love meeting consciousness in my heart — O beloved, know too the news of those separated, without a messenger.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The closing verse of the Śṛṅgāraśataka's central section. Three agents of love act: Kāma (desire speaking), the beloved (choosing), and the restless eye (acting spontaneously). At the moment where love's ocean meets consciousness — that is where the news of separation lives. The final line is an appeal to the beloved's own consciousness: know our state without a messenger — because true love requires no intermediary. At this depth, communication is direct.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: प्रेमाची काही इच्छा कामदेव सांगतो; काही प्रिया निवडते; काही चंचल नयन स्वतःच करतात. या क्षणी माझ्या हृदयात प्रेमसागराच्या संगमात — हे प्रिये, दूतीशिवायच विरहींची वार्ता तुलाही कळो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: प्रेमाचे तीन स्रोत — कामदेव, प्रिया, डोळे. आणि मग: या क्षणी हृदयात प्रेमाचा सागर. दूतीशिवाय वार्ता कळो. खऱ्या प्रेमाला दूत नको — ते थेट पोहोचतं. शृंगारशतकाचा हा समारोप — प्रेमाची थेट, मध्यस्थ-मुक्त ओळख.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
प्रसन्नः सर्वदेवेभ्यः प्रसन्नः सर्वभूतेषु ।
यत्र तत्र स्थितो नित्यं परितृप्तः स्वयंभुवः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Prasannaḥ sarvadevebhyaḥ prasannaḥ sarvabhūteṣu |
Yatra tatra sthito nityaṃ paritṛptaḥ svayambhuvaḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Gracious toward all gods; gracious toward all beings; wherever situated, always fulfilled — the self-born one.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A vision of the liberated person as permanently gracious — not as an achievement requiring effort but as a natural state. The svayambhu (self-born — one who is complete in themselves, not dependent on circumstances for their completeness) is gracious everywhere because they carry their completeness within. Wherever they are situated, they are fulfilled. This is the Śṛṅgāraśataka's most direct glimpse of the state that lies beyond desire — not the absence of love but love without need.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: सर्व देवांबद्दल प्रसन्न; सर्व प्राण्यांबद्दल प्रसन्न; जिथे असेल तिथे, नेहमी परितृप्त — स्वयंभू.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: स्वयंभू — स्वतःच पूर्ण. देवांबद्दल, प्राण्यांबद्दल, सगळ्यांबद्दल प्रसन्न. कुठेही असला तरी परितृप्त. कारण तृप्ती परिस्थितीवर नाही — आत आहे. शृंगारशतक येथे एका वेगळ्याच प्रेमाकडे पोहोचतं — ज्याला गरज नाही, पण ज्याला उबदारपणा आहे. हे प्रेम वैराग्याला जुडतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
सुवर्णपुष्पां पृथिवीं चिन्वन्ति पुरुषास्त्रयः ।
शूरश्च कृतविद्यश्च यश्च जानाति सेवितुम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Suvarṇapuṣpāṃ pṛthivīṃ cinvanti puruṣāstrāyaḥ |
Śūraśca kṛtavidyaśca yaśca jānāti sevitum ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Three types of persons gather the golden flowers of the earth: the brave, the truly learned, and the one who knows how to serve.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The closing verse of the Śṛṅgāraśataka — a verse of earthly aspiration and three paths to excellence. The golden flowers of the earth (wealth, honour, achievement) are gathered by three types: the brave (through action and courage), the truly learned (through knowledge and cultivation), and the one who knows how to serve (through intelligent, attentive service). The three are not ranked — all three paths are valid. The Śṛṅgāraśataka closes not with longing but with the affirmation of three ways to live well.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: तीन प्रकारचे लोक पृथ्वीची सुवर्णफुले गोळा करतात: शूर, खरोखर विद्वान, आणि सेवा करणं जाणणारा.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: तीन मार्ग — शौर्य, विद्या, सेवा. तिन्ही वेगळे, तिन्ही मौल्यवान. पृथ्वीवर यश मिळवण्याचे हे तीन मार्ग. भर्तृहरि शृंगारशतक इच्छेने सुरू केलं, ज्ञानाने जगलं, आणि या तीन मार्गांच्या सन्मानाने संपवतो. इच्छेच्या पलीकडे कर्म, ज्ञान, सेवा.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
शुभं करोति कल्याणमारोग्यं धनसम्पदः ।
शत्रुबुद्धिविनाशाय दीपज्योतिर्नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Śubhaṃ karoti kalyāṇamārogyaṃ dhanasaṃpadaḥ |
Śatrubuddhivināśāya dīpajyotirnamo'stu te ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: May you do good, bring welfare, health and wealth; may you destroy the enemies of the mind — salutation to you, O light of the lamp.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A benedictory verse in the devotional register — a salutation to the light (dīpa) that brings auspiciousness, health, wealth, and the destruction of the enemies of the mind (the inner enemies: desire, anger, delusion). In the Vairāgyaśataka, the lamp is not merely a physical object but a symbol of the inner light of knowledge that dispels darkness. The verse applies equally to the physical lamp lit at worship and to the inner lamp of awareness.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: शुभ करो, कल्याण करो, आरोग्य आणि धन-संपत्ती दे; शत्रूबुद्धीचा नाश करो — हे दीपज्योती, तुला नमस्कार.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: वैराग्यशतकाचा प्रारंभिक आशीर्वाद. दीपाला नमस्कार — शुभ, कल्याण, आरोग्य, धन, आणि शत्रूबुद्धीचा नाश. शत्रूबुद्धी म्हणजे आतले शत्रू — काम, क्रोध, मोह. दीप बाहेरचा असो वा आतला ज्ञानाचा — तो अंधार विनाशतो. भर्तृहरि येथून वैराग्याचा प्रवास सुरू करतो.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
तृष्णा छिन्धि भज क्षमां जहि मदं पापे रतिं मा कृथाः
सत्यं भाष सुखे दुःखे च समतां सर्वत्र चान्वेषय ।
भूतेष्वेव दयां कुरु प्रविमृश स्वाध्यायशास्त्रं सदा
सेवस्वोत्तममाश्रमं हित वचः कुर्वन् परेषां सदा ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Tṛṣṇā chindhi bhaja kṣamāṃ jahi madaṃ pāpe ratiṃ mā kṛthāḥ
Satyaṃ bhāṣa sukhe duḥkhe ca samatāṃ sarvatra cānveṣaya |
Bhūteṣveva dayāṃ kuru pravimṛśa svādhyāyaśāstraṃ sadā
sevasttvottamamāśramaṃ hita vacaḥ kurvan pareṣāṃ sadā ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Cut craving; cultivate patience; give up pride; do not take pleasure in sin; speak truth; seek equanimity in joy and sorrow; always show compassion to beings; contemplate scripture and self-study; serve the highest way of life; always speak words of benefit to others.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: Ten injunctions — the Vairāgyaśataka's most comprehensive ethical prescription. Each is a practice, not a principle: cut, cultivate, give up, do not, speak, seek, show, contemplate, serve, speak. All ten together form a complete programme of the renunciant life. Together they constitute what Bhartuhari means by vairāgya: not the withdrawal from the world but this active, disciplined, compassionate engagement with it from a position of inner freedom.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: तृष्णा तोड; क्षमा जोप; मद सोड; पापात प्रीती नको; सत्य बोल; सुख-दुःखात समता शोध; प्राण्यांवर दया कर; शास्त्र आणि स्वाध्याय नेहमी चिंतव; उत्तम आश्रम सेव; नेहमी दुसऱ्यांचे हित बोल.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: दहा आज्ञा — वैराग्याचा संपूर्ण कार्यक्रम. तोड, जोप, सोड, नको, बोल, शोध, कर, चिंतव, सेव, बोल. या दहा कृतींत वैराग्यशतकाचं सार. वैराग्य म्हणजे जगापासून पळणं नाही — हे सक्रिय, शिस्तबद्ध, करुणामय जगणं आहे — आतल्या स्वातंत्र्यातून.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
उत्तमं यत्नमास्थाय करोत्यर्थसमागमम् ।
देयं दातव्यमिति यः स पुमान् धन्यतां व्रजेत् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Uttamaṃ yatnamāsthāya karotyarthasamāgamam |
Deyaṃ dātavyamiti yaḥ sa pumān dhanyatāṃ vrajet ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: He who makes the highest effort to accumulate wealth — and then thinks "it is to be given; it must be given" — that person attains the state of the blessed.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about the right relationship to wealth within the Vairāgyaśataka. The renunciant does not refuse to earn — they make the highest effort to accumulate. But the purpose of accumulation is giving. The person who earns with the intention of giving — who sees accumulated wealth as held in trust for distribution — achieves the state of the blessed (dhanyatā). This is the Vairāgyaśataka's economics: earn fully, hold lightly, give readily.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: उत्तम प्रयत्नाने धन मिळवतो — आणि "हे द्यायला आहे, दिलं पाहिजे" असा विचार करतो — तो माणूस धन्यतेला पोहोचतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: कमवा — पण देण्यासाठी. पूर्ण प्रयत्नाने धन मिळवा, पण ते धरून ठेवण्यासाठी नाही — देण्यासाठी. जो हे जाणतो, तो धन्य. वैराग्यशतकाचं हे अर्थशास्त्र आहे: जमवा पूर्णपणे, धरा हळुवारपणे, द्या स्वेच्छेने.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
भ्रान्तं देशमनेकदुर्गविषमं प्राप्तं न किंचित् फलं
त्यक्त्वा जातिकुलाभिमानमुचितं सेवा कृता निष्फला ।
भुक्तं मानविवर्जितं परगृहेष्वाशङ्कया काकवत्
तृष्णे जृम्भसि पापकर्मपिशुने नाद्यापि संतुष्यसि ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Bhrāntaṃ deśamanekadurgaviṣamaṃ prāptaṃ na kiṃcit phalaṃ
Tyaktvā jātikullābhimānamucitaṃ sevā kṛtā niṣphalā |
Bhuktaṃ mānavivarjitaṃ paragṛheṣvāśaṃkayā kākavat
tṛṣṇe jṛmbhasi pāpakarmāppiśune nādyāpi santuṣyasi ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Many difficult lands have been wandered, yet no fruit gained. Giving up the pride proper to one's lineage, service was rendered — fruitlessly. In others' houses, eaten with suspicion like a crow, without dignity. O Craving, you vile informer of evil deeds — even now you are not satisfied.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: One of the most confessional verses in the entire śataka trilogy. Bhartuhari addresses Tṛṣṇā (craving) directly and lays out the evidence of the damage done: wandering, servitude, loss of dignity, eating at others' tables like a crow. And through all of this — Tṛṣṇā is still not satisfied. The verse is a turning point: this catalogue of futile service to craving is the case for giving it up entirely. The argument is made from personal experience.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: अनेक कठीण देश भटकलो, काहीच फळ नाही. कुळाचा अभिमान सोडून सेवा केली — निष्फळ. दुसऱ्यांच्या घरी कावळ्यासारखं संशयाने खाल्लं — मानाशिवाय. हे तृष्णे, पापकर्माची खबर देणाऱ्या — आजही तू समाधानी नाहीस.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: आयुष्यभराचं हिशेब. भटकणं — निष्फळ. सेवा — निष्फळ. दुसऱ्यांकडे खाणं — अपमानित. आणि तरीही तृष्णा समाधानी नाही. भर्तृहरि आत्मपरीक्षण करतो — आणि त्यातून वैराग्याचा निर्णय घेतो. हे प्रत्येकाची कथा आहे — आपण सगळ्यांनी भटकलो, सेवा केली, खाल्लं — पण तृष्णा तृप्त नाही.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
कालः कल्पितकल्पवृक्षनगरे सौभाग्यसम्पत्तरु-
र्विद्या धर्मपरागकेसरिमती कीर्त्याम्बरोपेत्य च ।
शीलादर्शमणिर्दयाजललवो वैराग्यसम्पत्सुमं
सन्तोषो भवतां सदा सुखकरो नित्यं जयत्वात्मनि ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kālaḥ kalpitakalpavṛkṣanagare saubhāgyasampattaru-
rvidyā dharmaparāgakesarimatī kīrtyambaropetya ca |
Śīlādarśamaṇirdayājalllavo vairāgyasampatssumaṃ
santoṣo bhavatāṃ sadā sukhakaro nityaṃ jayatvātmani ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: In the city of the imagined wish-fulfilling tree of time — let good fortune be the tree of prosperity; knowledge the pollen-bearing stamens of dharma; glory the sky surrounding; character the jewelled mirror; compassion the drop of water; renunciation the flower of wealth — and may contentment, always happiness-giving, always triumph in your self.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of elaborate metaphorical architecture — each quality of the good life is mapped onto a part of the kalpavṛkṣa city. The cumulative vision is of an inner kingdom where each virtue plays its role. The final line is the most important: may contentment (santoṣa) always triumph within the self (ātmani). All the other qualities are arranged around this one — contentment is the victory that makes all the rest possible.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: काळाच्या कल्पित कल्पवृक्ष-नगरात — सौभाग्य समृद्धीचा वृक्ष; विद्या धर्माच्या पराग-केसर; कीर्ती आकाश; शील आरसा-मणी; दया जलबिंदू; वैराग्य संपत्तीचं फूल — आणि संतोष सदा सुखदायक, तुमच्या आत नेहमी विजयी होवो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: एका आतल्या नगराचं चित्र. प्रत्येक गुण एका भागाचा रूपक. आणि त्या सगळ्यांचा विजय — संतोष. तो जिंकला तर बाकी सगळं जिंकलेलं. भर्तृहरिचं हे काव्यात्मक तत्त्वज्ञान — जगणं एका आतल्या नगरासारखं. त्याचा राजा: संतोष.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
कः शास्त्राणामपि मतिगतिः को दयालुः कृपालुः
को वा क्षान्तिः कविकुलगुरुः को गुणज्ञः सताम् च ।
इत्युच्चैस्तं परिपृच्छते प्रियमियं बाणस्य गोपायितं
वाचामेको विजयते कविकुलं भारवेरस्य मार्गः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Tāvad vibhāti kāvyeṣu nāṭakaṃ nāṭyajīvinām |
Yāvaccandro na coditaḥ sarasvatī bhagavatī ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Drama shines among poetic works for those who live by drama — only as long as the moon has not been summoned and the Goddess Saraswatī has not been invoked.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse about the transcendence of divine inspiration over craft. Drama — the highest of literary forms (as Bhartuhari noted earlier) — shines brilliantly. But its brilliance is conditional: it shines only until the moon of divine inspiration appears and Saraswatī is invoked. Once divine illumination enters, all craft is superseded. The verse makes a claim about the limits of technique: at a certain point, what matters is no longer the craft but the grace that moves through it.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: नाटकशास्त्रींसाठी काव्यात नाटक तेव्हापर्यंत शोभतं — जोपर्यंत चंद्र आला नाही आणि भगवती सरस्वतीची आवाहन झाली नाही.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: कला कौशल्य तोपर्यंत चमकतं जोपर्यंत दैवी प्रेरणा येत नाही. एकदा सरस्वती आली की सगळं कौशल्य त्यात विरतं. भर्तृहरि म्हणतो: तंत्र महत्त्वाचं — पण एका क्षणी कृपा सगळ्यावर मात करते. साधना कला शिकवते; कृपा कला जगवते.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
मेरुर्मन्दरचन्दनद्रुमवनं नागेन्द्रसिद्धाश्रमो
गङ्गा यमुना सरस्वती सरितां शेषोऽपि नागः पुनः ।
ध्यानं ज्ञानमजस्रमर्पितमनः शम्भोः पदं सेवितं
तीर्थं पापहरं हि पादतलयोर्मज्जत्यतः कीर्त्यते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Merurmandaracandanadrumavannaṃ nāgendrasiddhāśramo
Gaṅgā yamunā sarasvatī saritāṃ śeṣo'pi nāgaḥ punaḥ |
Dhyānaṃ jñānamajasramarpitamanaḥ śambhoḥ padaṃ sevitaṃ
tīrthaṃ pāpaharaṃ hi pādatalayor majjatyataḥ kīrtyate ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Meru, Mandara, sandalwood forests, the hermitage of the serpent-king Siddhas; the Ganges, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, and also Śeṣa the cosmic serpent; constant meditation, knowledge, with the mind surrendered, the feet of Śambhu served — the sin-removing pilgrimage-place is said to sink into the soles of the feet, from which it is proclaimed.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of sacred geography internalized. All the great holy places — mountains, rivers, hermitages — are not external destinations to be visited but internalized presences that sink into the soles of the feet of the one who has surrendered the mind in meditation. The yogi who meditates with surrendered mind at Śiva's feet carries all the tīrthas within. The outer pilgrimage is transcended by the inner one.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: मेरू, मंदार, चंदनवन, सिद्धाश्रम; गंगा, यमुना, सरस्वती, शेषनाग; सतत ध्यान, ज्ञान, समर्पित मन, शंभूचे पाद सेवन — सगळी पापहर तीर्थे अशा माणसाच्या पायाच्या तळात विराजमान होतात.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: बाहेरची तीर्थे आत येतात. जो मन समर्पित करून, ध्यान आणि ज्ञानाने शंभूची सेवा करतो — त्याच्या पायाखाली सगळी तीर्थे येतात. बाहेर जायची गरज नाही. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: आतल्या तीर्थाची किमत बाहेरच्या प्रवासापेक्षा अधिक.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
किं जप्येन तपस्यया किमुत च ध्यानेन योगेन किं
किं तीर्थेन किमिज्यया किमुत च श्रीखण्डलेपेन किम् ।
मर्यादारहितं मनः खलु यदि स्यान्नास्ति तत्साधनं
यद्युच्चैः प्रणमेद् गुरोश्चरणयोः तत्रैव सर्वं स्थितम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kiṃ japyena tapasyayā kimuta ca dhyānena yogena kiṃ
Kiṃ tīrthena kimijyayā kimuta ca śrīkhaṇḍalepena kim |
Maryādārahitaṃ manaḥ khalu yadi syānnāsti tatsāddhanaṃ
yadyuccaiḥ praṇamed guroḥ caraṇayoḥ tatraiva sarvaṃ sthitam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: What is the use of chanting, of austerity, of meditation, of yoga; what of pilgrimage, of ritual; what of sandalwood paste? If the mind is without discipline, none of these are means. But if one bows deeply to the feet of the teacher — in that alone everything dwells.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse that demolishes the entire apparatus of religious practice in a single movement — and then restores it, concentrated at one point. Chanting, austerity, meditation, yoga, pilgrimage, ritual, sandalwood — if the mind is undisciplined (maryādārahita — without boundary, without regulation), none of these achieve anything. But prostration before the teacher — with the regulated mind that genuine prostration requires — contains everything. The external practices are not dismissed but re-rooted: they work only when the mind is genuinely surrendered.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: जप, तप, ध्यान, योग; तीर्थ, पूजा, चंदन — कशाचा उपयोग, जर मन मर्यादाहीन असेल? पण जर गुरूच्या चरणांना खोलवर नमस्कार केला — तिथेच सगळं आहे.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: धर्माचं सगळं तंत्र एका प्रश्नात विरतं: मन नियंत्रित नसेल तर कशाचा उपयोग? आणि उत्तर: गुरूच्या चरणांना खरा नमस्कार — ज्यात मन खऱ्या अर्थाने झुकतं — त्यात सगळं आहे. बाहेरचं सगळं आतल्या एका क्षणात येतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
यस्तु संचरति देशान् याचनायै धनं प्रति ।
स्वयमेव हि संमानो यां तनोति स मान्यते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Kṣīṇāḥ kleśā yatasya manasaḥ saukhyam āgataṃ
Jñānam utpannam ajasraṃ samastha sarvatra ca |
Vairāgyaṃ sphūrtimattat paramam āptam idaṃ
dhanyatā so'sya pṛthvyāṃ yena niḥśreyasam āptam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: He whose mind's sorrows have diminished, who has attained happiness, whose knowledge has arisen continuously, who is equanimous everywhere; who has obtained the supreme flash of renunciation — he is the blessed one of the earth, who has attained the highest good.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A portrait of the blessed person — the jīvanmukta (one liberated in this life). The signs are: sorrows diminished (not absent, but diminished — the process is gradual), happiness arrived, knowledge arising continuously (not as a finished achievement but as a living stream), equanimity everywhere, and the supreme spark of vairāgya. This person has attained niḥśreyasa — the highest good — and is blessed on this earth, not in some imagined afterlife.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: ज्याच्या मनाचे क्लेश कमी झाले, सुख आलं, ज्ञान सतत उगवत आहे, सगळ्या ठिकाणी समभाव; ज्याला वैराग्याची परम स्फूर्ती मिळाली — तो पृथ्वीवर धन्य आहे, ज्याने सर्वोच्च श्रेय मिळवलं.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: जीवनमुक्ताचं चित्र. क्लेश कमी झाले, सुख आलं, ज्ञान वाहतं, समता, वैराग्याची स्फूर्ती — हे लक्षणे. आणि हे या जन्मात, या पृथ्वीवर. मरणानंतर नाही — आत्ता. भर्तृहरि सांगतो: मोक्ष भविष्यातला नाही — तो वर्तमानातला अनुभव आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
देहं दहति जाठरोऽनलः भुजङ्गो दहत्यन्तरात्मनः ।
तयोर्दाहकयोर्मध्ये कः शीतलिभविष्यति ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Dehaṃ dahati jāṭharo'nalaḥ bhujaṃgo dahatyantarātmanaḥ |
Tayordāhakayormadhye kaḥ śītalibhaviṣyati ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The digestive fire burns the body; the serpent (of desire) burns the inner self. Between these two fires — who will become cool?
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of compressed philosophical diagnosis. Two fires consume the human being: the external fire of hunger and digestion (jāṭhara agni — the fire of the stomach), which is physical and necessary; and the inner serpent of desire, which burns the self. Between these two — the necessity of physical existence and the torment of unfulfilled desire — genuine coolness (śītalī — peace, relief, the cooling of the inner heat) is very rare. The verse is not despairing but diagnostic: naming the situation is the first step toward addressing it.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: जाठराग्नी देह जाळतो; सर्पासारखी इच्छा अंतरात्मा जाळते. या दोन जाळणाऱ्यांमध्ये कोण थंड होईल?
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: दोन आग — एक बाहेरची (भूक, पाचनाग्नी), एक आतली (इच्छेचा साप). दोन्ही जाळतात. या दोन्हींच्या मध्ये खरी शांतता कुठे? — भर्तृहरि हे विचारतो, उत्तर देत नाही. उत्तर वाचकाने शोधायचं. आणि ते वैराग्यातच आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
उद्भूतं ज्ञानदीपेन प्रविष्टं परमं पदम् ।
नष्टा मोहतमःपुञ्जाः ज्ञानाग्नेर्दीप्ततेजसः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Udbhūtaṃ jñānadīpena praviṣṭaṃ paramaṃ padam |
Naṣṭā mohatmaḥpuñjāḥ jñānāgnerdīptatejasaḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Arisen through the lamp of knowledge, the supreme state is entered. The masses of delusion-darkness are destroyed by the blazing radiance of knowledge-fire.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of luminous affirmation. The lamp of knowledge (jñānadīpa) is the light that dispels moha (delusion). In its blazing radiance, the accumulated masses of delusion-darkness dissolve. This is not gradual improvement but sudden illumination — the darkness is destroyed (naṣṭa — finished, gone), and the supreme state (paramaṃ padam) is entered. Bhartuhari's vairāgya culminates not in withdrawal but in this blazing entry into light.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: ज्ञानदीपाने जागृत होऊन परम पद प्रविष्ट झालं. मोहाच्या अंधाराचे समूह ज्ञानाग्नीच्या तेजाने नष्ट झाले.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: ज्ञानाचा दीप — आणि अंधार संपतो. मोहाचे थर ज्ञानाग्नीत जळतात. परम पद — सर्वोच्च अवस्था — प्रवेश होतो. हे हळूहळू नाही — हे एका क्षणाचं उजाडणं. भर्तृहरिचं वैराग्य येथे पूर्ण होतं: सोडणं नाही — उजाडणं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
संसारसागरे घोरे विषयावर्तभीषणे ।
नमामि सद्गुरुं नावं नरकात्त्राणकारिणम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Saṃsārasāgare ghore viṣayāvartabhīṣaṇe |
Namāmi sadguruṃ nāvaṃ narakāt trāṇakāriṇam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: In the terrible ocean of worldly existence, terrifying with the whirlpools of sense objects — I salute the true teacher, the boat that saves from hell.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The gurustuti — salutation to the true teacher — as the means of crossing saṃsāra. The ocean is "ghora" (terrible, deep, dark) and the whirlpools of sense-objects are its particular danger — the vortices that pull the swimmer under. The sadguru is the nāvā — the boat. Not a distant deity but a practical means of crossing. Bhartuhari's most important salutation in the Vairāgyaśataka is to the teacher, not to the doctrine.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: घोर संसारसागरात, विषयांच्या आवर्तांनी भयानक — नरकातून तारणाऱ्या नौका असलेल्या सद्गुरूला मी नमस्कार करतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: संसार घोर, भयानक, विषयांच्या आवर्तांनी भरलेला. यातून तारतो कोण? — सद्गुरू. नौकेसारखा. भर्तृहरिचा सर्वात महत्त्वाचा नमस्कार — सिद्धान्ताला नाही, गुरूला. कारण वैराग्य एकट्याने होत नाही — त्याला जाणणाऱ्याची गरज असते.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
स्वप्नेऽपि यत् सुखं दुःखं तत् सत्यं परिकीर्तितम् ।
तदेव जाग्रतः सत्यं द्वयमेकत्र कारणम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Svapne'pi yat sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tat satyaṃ parikīrtitam |
Tadeva jāgrataḥ satyaṃ dvayamekatra kāraṇam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: Even what is experienced as happiness and sorrow in a dream is called real. That very thing is real for the one who is awake. Both have the same single cause.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of philosophical equivalence between dream and waking state. In a dream, joy and sorrow are completely real to the dreamer — they are experienced, not merely simulated. And in waking life, joy and sorrow are equally real. Both states have the same cause: the mind's projecting activity (the same consciousness dreaming and waking). The implication is Advaitic: if both dream and waking reality have the same cause (consciousness), then the distinction between them is relative, not absolute.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: स्वप्नातही जे सुख-दुःख आहे ते सत्य म्हणतात. तेच जागेपणीही सत्य आहे. दोन्हींचं एकच कारण.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: स्वप्न आणि जागेपण — दोन्हींत सुख-दुःख तेवढेच सत्य. दोन्हींचं कारण एकच: मन. मग जागे-झोपेचा फरक काय? — सापेक्ष, पूर्ण नाही. भर्तृहरि अद्वैताचा हा तर्क मांडतो: जर स्वप्न आणि जागेपण एकाच कारणातून येतात, तर खऱ्या अर्थाने फरक चेतनेतच आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
एकं सत् विप्रा बहुधा वदन्ति
अग्निं यमं मातरिश्वानमाहुः ।
इन्द्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुः
यद्यत्पश्यति तत्र तत्र स एव ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Ekaṃ sat viprā bahudhā vadanti
Agniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānamāhuḥ |
Indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimaāhuḥ
yadyatpaśyati tatra tatra sa eva ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The real is one — the learned speak of it in many ways. They call it Agni, Yama, Mātariśvan; they call it Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni. Whatever one sees, wherever one sees it — it is that one alone.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The great Ṛgvedic utterance (Ṛgveda 1.164.46 — "ekaṃ sat viprā bahudhā vadanti") quoted and extended by Bhartuhari. The One Reality is named differently by different traditions — all the Vedic devas are names of the same single Being. The final line is Bhartuhari's own addition: "whatever one sees, wherever — it is that one." The philosophical programme of the entire Vairāgyaśataka leads here: the multiplicity of appearances is the One Being under different names and forms.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: "एकमेव सत् — विद्वान अनेक प्रकारे वर्णन करतात." अग्नी, यम, मातरिश्वान; इंद्र, मित्र, वरुण — जे जे दिसतं, जिथे जिथे — ते तेच एक आहे.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: ऋग्वेदाचं महावाक्य — भर्तृहरि इथे उद्धृत करतो. एकच सत्य — अनेक नावे. देव वेगळे नाहीत — एकाच परम सत्याचे वेगवेगळे रूप. आणि जे जे दिसतं — ते तेच. अद्वैताचा हा अंतिम दृष्टिकोन: जगात कुठेही पाहा — एकाच चेतनेचं दर्शन.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
शिवः शक्तिः कामः क्षितिरथ रविः शीतकिरणः
स्मरो हंसः शक्रस्तदनु च परामर्शनमिति ।
अमी हृल्लेखाभिस्तिसृभिरवसानेषु घटिताः
भजन्ते वर्णास्तेत्रयोदश तिलकस्य विभुतम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Bhavati vilīnaṃ sarvaṃ yadā manaḥ svacchataṃ yāti |
Tad brahma paraṃ śudddhaṃ jyotīrūpaṃ mahādbhutam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: When everything dissolves and the mind attains purity — then that is the supreme Brahman, pure, of the form of light, most wondrous.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of experiential description of the supreme state. The moment of recognition is when "everything dissolves" — not annihilation but the dissolution of the false separations, the constructed identities, the accumulated stories. What remains is the mind in its natural purity — and that purity is itself the supreme Brahman, not a deity externally located but the pure light that the mind itself is when all its obscurations are removed. Most wondrous (mahādbhuta) — because it is right here, and yet it was hidden.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: जेव्हा सगळं विलीन होतं आणि मन स्वच्छता प्राप्त करतं — तेव्हा ते परम ब्रह्म असतं, शुद्ध, प्रकाशरूप, अत्यंत अद्भुत.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: मन शुद्ध झालं की ब्रह्म. बाहेर कुठे नाही — मनाच्या आत, शुद्धतेत. जेव्हा सगळ्या ओळखी विरतात, सगळे थर गळतात — तेव्हा जे राहतं ते प्रकाश आहे. तेच ब्रह्म. "अत्यंत अद्भुत" — कारण ते नेहमीच इथे होतं, फक्त झाकलेलं होतं.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
यत्र विश्वं न भवति यत्र विश्वमिदं स्थितम् ।
यत्र विश्वं लयं याति तत् पदं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Yatra viśvaṃ na bhavati yatra viśvamidaṃ sthitam |
Yatra viśvaṃ layaṃ yāti tat padaṃ brahma śāśvatam ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: That in which the universe is not; that in which this universe rests; that in which the universe dissolves — that state is the eternal Brahman.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: A verse of three-fold cosmic definition of Brahman — the origin, support, and dissolution of the universe in one. The universe does not exist in Brahman in the sense of being equal to it — Brahman transcends the universe. Yet the universe rests in Brahman. And the universe's dissolution is into Brahman. These three — creation, sustenance, dissolution — are the trikāla (three times) of Brahman's relationship to the universe. The "eternal state" (śāśvataṃ padam) is beyond all three.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: ज्यात विश्व नाही; ज्यात हे विश्व राहते; ज्यात विश्व विलीन होते — ते पद म्हणजे शाश्वत ब्रह्म.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: तीन संबंध: विश्वाच्या आधी, विश्वाच्या दरम्यान, विश्वाच्या नंतर — सगळ्यांत ब्रह्म. सृष्टी, स्थिती, लय — तिन्हींचं आधारतत्त्व. ते स्वतः या तिन्हींपलीकडे आहे — शाश्वत. भर्तृहरिचं हे ब्रह्माचं वर्णन कालातीत आहे.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः ।
अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye'sya hṛdi śritāḥ |
Atha martyo'mṛto bhavatyatra brahma samaśnute ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: When all the desires that dwell in the heart are released — then the mortal becomes immortal, and here attains Brahman.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The Kaṭhopaniṣad (II.3.14) quoted in the Vairāgyaśataka — "yadā sarve pramucyante kāmāḥ" — one of the most celebrated utterances in the Upaniṣads. The condition for immortality is the release of all desires that dwell in the heart. Not suppression, not renunciation through willpower, but the natural falling away of desires when the truth is known. And "here" — atra, in this life, in this body, at this moment — not in some afterlife. The mortal becomes immortal here. This is the Vairāgyaśataka's penultimate word.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: जेव्हा हृदयात राहणाऱ्या सगळ्या इच्छा मुक्त होतात — तेव्हा मर्त्य अमर बनतो, आणि इथेच ब्रह्म प्राप्त होतं.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: कठोपनिषदाचं हे महावचन भर्तृहरि वैराग्यशतकात ठेवतो. इच्छा जेव्हा गळतात — जबरदस्तीने नाही, सत्य जाणल्यावर आपोआप — तेव्हा मर्त्य अमर होतो. आणि "इथे" — या जन्मात, या देहात. मृत्यूनंतर नाही — आत्ता. भर्तृहरिचं हे अंतिम आश्वासन.

SUBHASHITS.deva:
चिदाकाशं परं ब्रह्म सर्वत्र समवस्थितम् ।
स्वयं प्रकाशमानं तद् ज्ञात्वा मुक्तो भवेन्नरः ॥
SUBHASHITS.translit:
Cidākāśaṃ paraṃ brahma sarvatra samavasthitam |
Svayaṃ prakāśamānaṃ tad jñātvā mukto bhavennaraḥ ||
SUBHASHITS.meaningEn: The space of consciousness — the supreme Brahman — is equally established everywhere; self-luminous. Knowing that, the person becomes liberated.
SUBHASHITS.explanationEn: The final verse of the entire Bhartuhari Subhashita Saṃgraha — three hundred verses, three śatakas, one life's journey. The last word is cidākāśa — the space of consciousness, the luminous infinite awareness that is the supreme Brahman. It is everywhere equally (sarvatra samavasthitam). It is self-luminous — it does not need an external light to illuminate it; it is itself the light by which all else is seen. Knowing this — not intellectually but in direct recognition — the person becomes liberated. This is Bhartuhari's final, complete word: the very awareness that reads these words, that thinks these thoughts, that loves and suffers and renounces — is itself the supreme light. Know that, and be free.
SUBHASHITS.meaningMr: चिदाकाश — परमब्रह्म — सर्वत्र समभावाने स्थित आहे; स्वयंप्रकाशित. ते जाणल्याने माणूस मुक्त होतो.
SUBHASHITS.explanationMr: भर्तृहरि सुभाषित संग्रहाचा अंतिम श्लोक. तीनशे श्लोक, तीन शतके, एक आयुष्याचा प्रवास — आणि शेवटी एक वाक्य: चिदाकाश सगळ्या ठिकाणी स्वयंप्रकाशित आहे. जे वाचतं, जे विचार करतं, जे प्रेम करतं, जे त्याग करतं — तीच चेतना परमब्रह्म आहे. ते जाणलं की मुक्ती. हे भर्तृहरिचं अंतिम, संपूर्ण वचन: तू तेच आहेस — जाण आणि मुक्त हो.

INTRO.title: The Living Tree
INTRO.subtitle: How Indian knowledge grew from the Vedas into the classical corpus
INTRO.note: Original synthesis for Bhāratīya Jñāna Bhaṇḍāra. Dates are scholarly approximations; the tradition itself is more interested in continuity than in calendars.
lede: A library can show you what a civilization knew. It is harder to show how it came to know it — and harder still to convey the most interesting thing of all: that none of this was planned. No committee sat down to design Āyurveda, or grammar, or algebra, or the philosophy of the self. Each grew out of the one before it, often as a by-product of solving a much smaller, more practical problem. The story of the Indic corpus is the story of a single thread of curiosity that never broke — and that, every few centuries, branched into something the previous generation could not have imagined.

This is a map of that branching. Read it, and the catalogue below stops being a list of unfamiliar Sanskrit titles and becomes what it actually is: the record of a three-thousand-year conversation that human beings were having with the cosmos, with each other, and with themselves.

sections.title: The beginning was wonder, not religion
paragraphs: The oldest layer, the Ṛgveda, does not read like a holy book. It reads like the notebook of people who could not stop looking up. Dawn (Uṣas) arrives and someone needs to say what it is like. Fire (Agni) is the one thing that turns the raw into the cooked and carries the offering upward, so it deserves the first hymn. There is a verse — the Nāsadīya Sūkta — that asks how the universe began and then, astonishingly, admits that perhaps no one knows, perhaps not even the gods, perhaps not even that one who looks down from the highest heaven.

That is the founding gesture of the whole tradition: a question held open rather than closed. The motive at the root was not obedience. It was comprehension — the wish to stand in a right relationship with forces vastly larger than oneself, and to articulate that relationship in language exact enough to be worth repeating.

The other three Vedas are already specialisations of that single impulse. The Yajurveda is the working handbook of the ritual — what to say and do, and in what order. The Sāmaveda sets the hymns to melody and is, quite literally, the oldest surviving musical notation on earth. The Atharvaveda comes down from the priests to the household: it is medicine, charm, anxiety and cure, the distant ancestor of every later Indic science of healing.
sections.pullQuote: The four Vedas are not four books but four uses of one impulse — knowing, doing, singing, healing.

sections.title: How preservation accidentally invented the sciences
paragraphs: Here is the pivot that almost no popular account gets right, and it is the most interesting part of the entire story. The Veda was oral. It had to be transmitted across centuries with not a single syllable lost — because a mispronounced mantra was thought to be not merely incorrect but ineffective, even dangerous. This is an extraordinary engineering problem: how do you transmit a large body of text, perfectly, for a thousand years, with no paper?

Solving that one problem set off a chain reaction. To preserve the Veda, you had to build the disciplines that guard it — the six Vedāṅgas, the “limbs of the Veda.” And in building them, the tradition stumbled into the sciences: phonetics (Śikṣā), the most rigorous the pre-modern world would see; ritual geometry (Kalpa and the Śulba-sūtras), the oldest Indian mathematics, including the relation we now call Pythagoras’ theorem; grammar (Vyākaraṇa), which produced Pāṇini’s Aṣṭādhyāyī, a complete generative grammar of Sanskrit twenty-five centuries before Chomsky; etymology (Nirukta); prosody (Chandas), whose analysis of metre gave the world a binary notation and the sequence Europe would later call Fibonacci’s; and astronomy (Jyotiṣa), from which came the calendar and eclipse prediction.

This is the through-line worth pressing on: in India, the empirical sciences were born as the servants of the sacred, and then quietly outgrew their master. Geometry began as altar-building. Astronomy began as ritual timekeeping. Linguistics began as the wish to say a prayer correctly. The practical and the profound were never separated — which is exactly why the knowledge stayed connected to life.
sections.pullQuote: Six disciplines invented to protect a text — and one of them turned out to be the first formal grammar in human history.

sections.title: From the altar to the self
paragraphs: By roughly the middle of the first millennium BCE, the conversation changed direction. The Upaniṣads — literally “sitting down near” a teacher — are the end of the Veda (Vedānta), and they turn away from the ritual fire toward an even harder fire: the questioner himself.

The motive shifts from prosperity to liberation (mokṣa). The questions are no longer “how do I perform the sacrifice?” but “who is the one performing it?” Who am I, beneath the name and the body? What is real when everything changes? The answer the Upaniṣads keep circling — tat tvam asi, “you are that” — is among the boldest claims any culture has made: that the innermost self (ātman) and the ultimate reality (brahman) are one.

What matters for the story is the method. These are dialogues — a boy and his father, a king and a sage, a woman, Gārgī, pressing a teacher until he tells her to stop or her head will fall off. Knowledge here is not handed down; it is won, by argument, in conversation. That habit of disciplined disagreement is about to become the engine of everything that follows.
sections.pullQuote: Knowledge here is not handed down; it is won, by argument, in conversation.

sections.title: The classical systematisation
paragraphs: The Upaniṣads ask the great questions but do not answer them systematically. The classical era — roughly the centuries on either side of the start of the Common Era — is when the tradition decided that questions this important deserved rigour. The result is the six āstika darśanas, the “viewpoints” or schools of philosophy, and they read like a faculty of a single ancient university:

Nyāya, logic and epistemology — what counts as valid knowledge, and how do you prove anything? Vaiśeṣika, natural philosophy — matter made of indivisible atoms (aṇu). Sāṅkhya, a complete enumeration of reality into consciousness (puruṣa) and nature (prakṛti). Yoga, the laboratory that takes Sāṅkhya’s map and walks it. Mīmāṃsā, the science of interpretation — the ancestor of Indian legal reasoning. And Vedānta, the return to the Upaniṣadic question of the self, now argued school by school.

What drove this systematisation was a culture of public debate (śāstrārtha). Schools, including the dissenting ones, met and argued in the open, and the loser was expected to concede. You cannot win such debates with assertion; you need airtight definitions, rules of evidence, theories of error. So India produced one of the world’s great traditions of logic and epistemology — not in spite of its spirituality, but because its spirituality was willing to be questioned.
sections.pullQuote: Six schools, one debating hall. Disagreement was not a threat to the tradition — it was the method.

sections.title: The dissenters who made the tradition stronger
paragraphs: No account is honest if it pretends the corpus was a single harmonious voice. Running alongside the orthodox schools were the nāstika darśanas — the three that declined the authority of the Veda: Cārvāka, thoroughgoing materialists who insisted on the evidence of the senses and laughed at the afterlife; Bauddha, the vast intellectual world of Buddhism, which produced in Dignāga and Dharmakīrti some of the sharpest logicians the subcontinent ever saw; and Jaina, the Jains, whose doctrine of anekāntavāda — “many-sidedness” — is a remarkable early theory of intellectual humility: every viewpoint is partial, so hold your own with a syāt, a “perhaps.”

This is the part to celebrate rather than hide. The dissent enriched the whole. Buddhist logic forced Hindu logic to become more precise; the Jain insistence on non-violence and many-sidedness pushed an entire civilization toward tolerance and vegetarian ethics; the Cārvāka materialists kept everyone honest about evidence. A tradition that can argue with itself for two thousand years and stay in one conversation is not fragile. It is alive.
sections.pullQuote: A tradition that can argue with itself for two thousand years and stay in one conversation is not fragile. It is alive.

sections.title: Knowledge turned to living — the applied sciences and the śāstras
paragraphs: Once the philosophical foundations were laid, the same rigour was pointed back at ordinary life. The Upavedas are the applied sciences, each attached to one of the four Vedas: Āyurveda, medicine — Caraka and Suśruta turning healing into a system of diagnosis, surgery and prevention; Dhanurveda, the science of war and the disciplined body; Gāndharvaveda, music and the performing arts; Sthāpatyaveda, architecture and the ordering of built space.

And the śāstras are the manuals for living well together: Dharma-śāstra, ethics and civil law (Manu, Yājñavalkya); Artha-śāstra, Kauṭilya’s coldly brilliant manual of statecraft, economics, taxation and intelligence; Kāma-śāstra, pleasure, relationship and the art of living, treated as a subject worthy of study; and the Nāṭya-śāstra with the Kāvya poets — a complete science of drama, beauty and rasa, the emotion a work of art evokes.

Behind all of this sits the most quietly radical idea of the tradition: the four puruṣārthas, the legitimate aims of a human life — dharma (ethics), artha (prosperity), kāma (pleasure and love), and mokṣa (freedom). A culture that gives prosperity and pleasure their own sciences, alongside ethics and liberation, is not world-denying. It is trying to teach you how to live a whole life.
sections.pullQuote: A culture that gives prosperity and pleasure their own sciences is not world-denying. It is trying to teach you how to live a whole life.

sections.title: The democratisation of wisdom
paragraphs: So far this is a tradition of specialists, conducted largely in Sanskrit. The genius of the next phase is that it gave the same wisdom to everyone. The Itihāsa — the two epics, Rāmāyaṇa and Mahābhārata — and the Purāṇas took the abstractions of philosophy and dissolved them into story, so that a farmer who would never read the Upaniṣads could absorb their ethics over a lifetime of evenings. Inside the Mahābhārata sits the Bhagavad-gītā, which gathers the rival paths — action, knowledge, devotion — and shows they are one mountain climbed from different sides.

Then, from around the sixth century, came the Bhakti movements — the moral high point of the whole story. The Ālvārs and Nāyanārs in the Tamil south, the Vārkarī tradition in Maharashtra, the Sants of the north, all made the same revolutionary move: they sang of the divine in the language of ordinary people, and declared that liberation was open to all — regardless of caste, of gender, of learning. In Maharashtra, Dnyaneshwar poured the Sanskrit Gītā into living Marathi so that his neighbours could drink from it; Tukaram, Janabai and Namdev turned the highest metaphysics into songs you could sing while grinding grain.

This is what “progressive and enriching” actually looks like in history: a body of knowledge that began as the closely guarded property of a priesthood, and over two thousand years deliberately handed itself down — to the philosopher, then to the storyteller’s audience, then to the unlettered devotee singing in her own tongue.
sections.pullQuote: The arc is Sanskrit → vernacular → everyone. This is the emotional core of the library.

sections.title: The scientific golden age, and the long re-reading
paragraphs: Two final movements complete the tree. During the same classical and early-medieval centuries, the abstract love of number matured into a golden age of mathematics and astronomy. Āryabhaṭa proposed that the earth turns; Brahmagupta gave the world its rules for zero and negative numbers; Bhāskara wrote of the infinitely small; and the Kerala school, centuries before Newton, summed infinite series for the trigonometric functions. The decimal place-value system and the numeral for zero — arguably India’s single largest gift to the practical life of every human being now alive — flowed out from here to the Arab world and then to Europe.

And then, under colonial rule and after, came the modern re-reading — Rammohan Roy, Vivekananda, Tagore, Aurobindo, Gandhi, Ambedkar, Krishnamurti — thinkers who took the entire inherited corpus and read it again, critically, for a new age: keeping what gives life, challenging what does not. That re-reading is not the end of the tradition. It is simply its latest branch, and it proves the thing this whole map has been arguing: the tree is still growing.
sections.pullQuote: The modern thinkers are participants in the same conversation, not a break from it.

conclusion.title: Why it kept enriching human life
conclusion.intro: If you take only four things from this, let them be these.

threads.label: One — knowledge was never cut off from life.
threads.text: Geometry served the altar, medicine served the body, ethics served the village. Even the most rarefied metaphysics was meant to be practised, not merely believed. A tradition built this way does not produce knowledge that gathers dust.

threads.label: Two — it advanced by argument, not by decree.
threads.text: From Gārgī’s questions to the open debating halls of the classical schools to the materialists who denied the afterlife, disagreement was the engine. The corpus is large precisely because it refused to settle.

threads.label: Three — it kept opening its doors.
threads.text: The long movement from priestly Sanskrit to the devotional song of an unlettered saint is one of the great democratisations of wisdom in world history — and it happened from within, by choice.

threads.label: Four — it held the whole human being in view.
threads.text: Prosperity, pleasure, ethics and freedom each got their own science. The aim was never renunciation alone, nor success alone, but a life lived fully on every level at once — which is, in the end, simply another word for happiness.

INTRO.closing: That is the invitation of this library. Not a museum of a finished past, but the living record of people who asked the largest questions they could, refused easy answers, and passed the conversation forward — to us.
